Proverbs 10:1.title: Proverbs 10:1
Proverbs 10:1.content: The comfort of parents much depends on their children; and this suggests to both, motives to their duties.

Proverbs 10:2.title: Proverbs 10:2, 3
Proverbs 10:2.content: Though the righteous may be poor, the Lord will not suffer him to want what is needful for spiritual life.

Proverbs 10:3.title: Proverbs 10:2, 3
Proverbs 10:3.content: Though the righteous may be poor, the Lord will not suffer him to want what is needful for spiritual life.

Proverbs 10:4.title: Proverbs 10:4
Proverbs 10:4.content: Those who are fervent in spirit, serving the Lord, are likely to be rich in faith, and rich in good works.

Proverbs 10:5.title: Proverbs 10:5
Proverbs 10:5.content: Here is just blame of those who trifle away opportunities, both for here and for hereafter.

Proverbs 10:6.title: Proverbs 10:6
Proverbs 10:6.content: Abundance of blessings shall abide on good men; real blessings.

Proverbs 10:7.title: Proverbs 10:7
Proverbs 10:7.content: Both the just and the wicked must die; but between their souls there is a vast difference.

Proverbs 10:8.title: Proverbs 10:8
Proverbs 10:8.content: The wise in heart puts his knowledge in practice.

Proverbs 10:9.title: Proverbs 10:9
Proverbs 10:9.content: Dissemblers, after all their shuffling, will be exposed.

Proverbs 10:10.title: Proverbs 10:10
Proverbs 10:10.content: Trick and artifice will be no excuse for iniquity.

Proverbs 10:11.title: Proverbs 10:11
Proverbs 10:11.content: The good man's mouth is always open to teach, comfort, and correct others.

Proverbs 10:12.title: Proverbs 10:12
Proverbs 10:12.content: Where there is hatred, every thing stirs up strife. By bearing with each other, peace and harmony are preserved.

Proverbs 10:13.title: Proverbs 10:13
Proverbs 10:13.content: Those that foolishly go on in wicked ways, prepare rods for themselves.

Proverbs 10:14.title: Proverbs 10:14
Proverbs 10:14.content: Whatever knowledge may be useful, we must lay it up, that it may not be to seek when we want it. The wise gain this wisdom by reading, by hearing the word, by meditation, by prayer, by faith in Christ, who is made of God unto us wisdom.

Proverbs 10:15.title: Proverbs 10:15
Proverbs 10:15.content: This refers to the common mistakes both of rich and poor, as to their outward condition. Rich people's wealth exposes them to many dangers; while a poor man may live comfortably, if he is content, keeps a good conscience, and lives by faith.

Proverbs 10:16.title: Proverbs 10:16
Proverbs 10:16.content: Perhaps a righteous man has no more than what he works hard for, but that labour tends to life.

Proverbs 10:17.title: Proverbs 10:17
Proverbs 10:17.content: The traveller that has missed his way, and cannot bear to be told of it, and to be shown the right way, must err still.

Proverbs 10:18.title: Proverbs 10:18
Proverbs 10:18.content: He is especially a fool who thinks to hide anything from God; and malice is no better.

Proverbs 10:19.title: Proverbs 10:19
Proverbs 10:19.content: Those that speak much, speak much amiss. He that checks himself is a wise man, and therein consults his own peace.

Proverbs 10:20.title: Proverbs 10:20, 21
Proverbs 10:20.content: The tongue of the just is sincere, freed from the dross of guile and evil design. Pious discourse is spiritual food to the needy. Fools die for want of a heart, so the word is; for want of thought.

Proverbs 10:21.title: Proverbs 10:20, 21
Proverbs 10:21.content: The tongue of the just is sincere, freed from the dross of guile and evil design. Pious discourse is spiritual food to the needy. Fools die for want of a heart, so the word is; for want of thought.

Proverbs 10:22.title: Proverbs 10:22
Proverbs 10:22.content: That wealth which is truly desirable, has no vexation of spirit in the enjoyment; no grief for the loss; no guilt by the abuse of it. What comes from the love of God, has the grace of God for its companion.

Proverbs 10:23.title: Proverbs 10:23
Proverbs 10:23.content: Only foolish and wicked men divert themselves with doing harm to others, or tempting to sin.

Proverbs 10:24.title: Proverbs 10:24
Proverbs 10:24.content: The largest desire of eternal blessings the righteous can form, will be granted.

Proverbs 10:25.title: Proverbs 10:25
Proverbs 10:25.content: The course of prosperous sinners is like a whirlwind, which soon spends itself, and is gone.

Proverbs 10:26.title: Proverbs 10:26
Proverbs 10:26.content: As vinegar sets the teeth on edge, and as the smoke causes the eyes to smart, so the sluggard vexes his employer.

Proverbs 10:27.title: Proverbs 10:27, 28
Proverbs 10:27.content: What man is he that loves life? Let him fear God, and that will secure to him life enough in this world, and eternal life in the other.

Proverbs 10:28.title: Proverbs 10:27, 28
Proverbs 10:28.content: What man is he that loves life? Let him fear God, and that will secure to him life enough in this world, and eternal life in the other.

Proverbs 10:29.title: Proverbs 10:29
Proverbs 10:29.content: The believer grows stronger in faith, and obeys with increased delight.

Proverbs 10:30.title: Proverbs 10:30
Proverbs 10:30.content: The wicked would be glad to have this earth their home for ever, but it cannot be so. They must die and leave all their idols behind.

Proverbs 10:31.title: Proverbs 10:31, 32
Proverbs 10:31.content: A good man discourses wisely for the benefit of others. But it is the sin, and will be the ruin of a wicked man, that he speaks what is displeasing to God, and provoking to those he converses with. The righteous is kept by the power of God; and nothing shall be able to separate him from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus. Proverbs

Proverbs 10:32.title: Proverbs 10:31, 32
Proverbs 10:32.content: A good man discourses wisely for the benefit of others. But it is the sin, and will be the ruin of a wicked man, that he speaks what is displeasing to God, and provoking to those he converses with. The righteous is kept by the power of God; and nothing shall be able to separate him from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus. Proverbs

Proverbs 11:1.title: Proverbs 11:1
Proverbs 11:1.content: However men may make light of giving short weight or measure, and however common such crimes may be, they are an abomination to the Lord.

Proverbs 11:2.title: Proverbs 11:2
Proverbs 11:2.content: Considering how safe, and quiet, and easy the humble are, we see that with the lowly is wisdom.

Proverbs 11:3.title: Proverbs 11:3
Proverbs 11:3.content: An honest man's principles are fixed, therefore his way is plain.

Proverbs 11:4.title: Proverbs 11:4
Proverbs 11:4.content: Riches will stand men in no stead in the day of death.

Proverbs 11:5.title: Proverbs 11:5, 6
Proverbs 11:5.content: The ways of wickedness are dangerous. And sin will be its own punishment.

Proverbs 11:6.title: Proverbs 11:5, 6
Proverbs 11:6.content: The ways of wickedness are dangerous. And sin will be its own punishment.

Proverbs 11:7.title: Proverbs 11:7
Proverbs 11:7.content: When a godly man dies, all his fears vanish; but when a wicked man dies, his hopes vanish.

Proverbs 11:8.title: Proverbs 11:8
Proverbs 11:8.content: The righteous are often wonderfully kept from going into dangerous situations, and the ungodly go in their stead.

Proverbs 11:9.title: Proverbs 11:9
Proverbs 11:9.content: Hypocrites delude men into error and sin by artful objections against the truths of God's word.

Proverbs 11:10.title: Proverbs 11:10, 11
Proverbs 11:10.content: Nations prosper when wicked men are cast down.

Proverbs 11:11.title: Proverbs 11:10, 11
Proverbs 11:11.content: Nations prosper when wicked men are cast down.

Proverbs 11:12.title: Proverbs 11:12
Proverbs 11:12.content: A man of understanding does not judge of others by their success.

Proverbs 11:13.title: Proverbs 11:13
Proverbs 11:13.content: A faithful man will not disclose what he is trusted with, unless the honour of God and the real good of society require it.

Proverbs 11:14.title: Proverbs 11:14
Proverbs 11:14.content: We shall often find it to our advantage to advise with others.

Proverbs 11:15.title: Proverbs 11:15
Proverbs 11:15.content: The welfare of our families, our own peace, and our ability to pay just debts, must not be brought into danger. But here especially let us consider the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ in becoming Surety even for enemies.

Proverbs 11:16.title: Proverbs 11:16
Proverbs 11:16.content: A pious and discreet woman will keep esteem and respect, as strong men keep possession of wealth.

Proverbs 11:17.title: Proverbs 11:17
Proverbs 11:17.content: A cruel, froward, ill-natured man, is vexatious to those that are, and should be to him as his own flesh, and punishes himself.

Proverbs 11:18.title: Proverbs 11:18
Proverbs 11:18.content: He that makes it his business to do good, shall have a reward, as sure to him as eternal truth can make it.

Proverbs 11:19.title: Proverbs 11:19
Proverbs 11:19.content: True holiness is true happiness. The more violent a man is in sinful pursuits, the more he hastens his own destruction.

Proverbs 11:20.title: Proverbs 11:20
Proverbs 11:20.content: Nothing is more hateful to God, than hypocrisy and double dealing, which are here signified. God delights in such as aim and act with uprightness.

Proverbs 11:21.title: Proverbs 11:21
Proverbs 11:21.content: Joining together in sin shall not protect the sinners.

Proverbs 11:22.title: Proverbs 11:22
Proverbs 11:22.content: Beauty is abused by those who have not discretion or modesty with it. This is true of all bodily endowments.

Proverbs 11:23.title: Proverbs 11:23
Proverbs 11:23.content: The wicked desire mischief to others, but it shall return upon themselves.

Proverbs 11:24.title: Proverbs 11:24
Proverbs 11:24.content: A man may grow poor by not paying just debts, not relieving the poor, not allowing needful expenses. Let men be ever so saving of what they have, if God appoints, it comes to nothing.

Proverbs 11:25.title: Proverbs 11:25
Proverbs 11:25.content: Both in temporal and spiritual things, God commonly deals with his people according to the measure by which they deal with their brethren.

Proverbs 11:26.title: Proverbs 11:26
Proverbs 11:26.content: We must not hoard up the gifts of God's bounty, merely for our own advantage.

Proverbs 11:27.title: Proverbs 11:27
Proverbs 11:27.content: Seeking mischief is here set against seeking good; for those that are not doing good are doing hurt, even to themselves.

Proverbs 11:28.title: Proverbs 11:28
Proverbs 11:28.content: The true believer is a branch of the living Vine. When those that take root in the world wither, those who are grafted into Christ shall be fruitful.

Proverbs 11:29.title: Proverbs 11:29
Proverbs 11:29.content: He that brings trouble upon himself and his family, by carelessness, or by wickedness, shall be unable to keep and enjoy what he gets, as a man is unable to hold the wind, or to satisfy himself with it.

Proverbs 11:30.title: Proverbs 11:30
Proverbs 11:30.content: The righteous are as trees of life; and their influence upon earth, like the fruits of that tree, support and nourish the spiritual life in many.

Proverbs 11:31.title: Proverbs 11:31
Proverbs 11:31.content: Even the righteous, when they offend on earth, shall meet with sharp corrections; much more will the wicked meet the due reward of their sins. Let us then seek those blessings which our Surety purchased by his sufferings and death; let us seek to copy his example, and to keep his commandments. Proverbs

Proverbs 12:1.title: Proverbs 12:1
Proverbs 12:1.content: Those who have grace, will delight in the instructions given them. Those that stifle their convictions, are like brutes.

Proverbs 12:2.title: Proverbs 12:2
Proverbs 12:2.content: The man who covers selfish and vicious designs under a profession of religion or friendship, will be condemned.

Proverbs 12:3.title: Proverbs 12:3
Proverbs 12:3.content: Though men may advance themselves by sinful arts, they cannot settle and secure themselves. But those who by faith are rooted in Christ, are firmly fixed.

Proverbs 12:4.title: Proverbs 12:4
Proverbs 12:4.content: A wife who is pious, prudent, and looks well to the ways of her household, who makes conscience of her duty, and can bear crosses; such a one is an honour and comfort to her husband. She that is the reverse of this, preys upon him, and consumes him.

Proverbs 12:5.title: Proverbs 12:5
Proverbs 12:5.content: Thoughts are not free; they are under the Divine knowledge, therefore under the Divine command. It is a man's shame to act with deceit, with trick and design.

Proverbs 12:6.title: Proverbs 12:6
Proverbs 12:6.content: Wicked people speak mischief to their neighbours. A man may sometimes do a good work with one good word.

Proverbs 12:7.title: Proverbs 12:7
Proverbs 12:7.content: God's blessing is often continued to the families of godly men, while the wicked are overthrown.

Proverbs 12:8.title: Proverbs 12:8
Proverbs 12:8.content: The apostles showed wisdom by glorying in shame for the name of Christ.

Proverbs 12:9.title: Proverbs 12:9
Proverbs 12:9.content: He that lives in a humble state, who has no one to wait upon him, but gets bread by his own labour, is happier than he that glories in high birth or gay attire, and wants necessaries.

Proverbs 12:10.title: Proverbs 12:10
Proverbs 12:10.content: A godly man would not put even an animal to needless pain. But the wicked often speak of others as well used, when they would not endure like treatment for a single day.

Proverbs 12:11.title: Proverbs 12:11
Proverbs 12:11.content: It is men's wisdom to mind their business, and follow an honest calling. But it is folly to neglect business; and the grace of God teaches men to disdain nothing but sin.

Proverbs 12:12.title: Proverbs 12:12
Proverbs 12:12.content: When the ungodly see others prosper by sin, they wish they could act in the same way. But the root of Divine grace, in the heart of the righteous, produces other desires and purposes.

Proverbs 12:13.title: Proverbs 12:13
Proverbs 12:13.content: Many a man has paid dear in this world for the transgression of his lips.

Proverbs 12:14.title: Proverbs 12:14
Proverbs 12:14.content: When men use their tongues aright, to teach and comfort others, they enjoy acceptance through Christ Jesus; and the testimony of their conscience, that they in some measure answer the end of their being.

Proverbs 12:15.title: Proverbs 12:15
Proverbs 12:15.content: A fool, in the sense of Scripture, means a wicked man, one who acts contrary to the wisdom that is from above. His rule is, to do what is right in his own eyes.

Proverbs 12:16.title: Proverbs 12:16
Proverbs 12:16.content: A foolish man is soon angry, and is hasty in expressing it; he is ever in trouble and running into mischief. It is kindness to ourselves to make light of injuries and affronts, instead of making the worst of them.

Proverbs 12:17.title: Proverbs 12:17
Proverbs 12:17.content: It is good for all to dread and detest the sin of lying, and to be governed by honesty.

Proverbs 12:18.title: Proverbs 12:18
Proverbs 12:18.content: Whisperings and evil surmises, like a sword, separate those that have been dear to each other. The tongue of the wise is health, making all whole.

Proverbs 12:19.title: Proverbs 12:19
Proverbs 12:19.content: If truth be spoken, it will hold good; whoever may be disobliged, still it will keep its ground.

Proverbs 12:20.title: Proverbs 12:20
Proverbs 12:20.content: Deceit and falsehood bring terrors and perplexities. But those who consult the peace and happiness of others have joy in their own minds.

Proverbs 12:21.title: Proverbs 12:21
Proverbs 12:21.content: If men are sincerely righteous, the righteous God has engaged that no evil shall happen to them. But they that delight in mischief shall have enough of it.

Proverbs 12:22.title: Proverbs 12:22
Proverbs 12:22.content: Make conscience of truth, not only in words, but in actions.

Proverbs 12:23.title: Proverbs 12:23
Proverbs 12:23.content: Foolish men proclaim to all the folly and emptiness of their minds.

Proverbs 12:24.title: Proverbs 12:24
Proverbs 12:24.content: Those who will not take pains in an honest calling, living by tricks and dishonesty, are paltry and beggarly.

Proverbs 12:25.title: Proverbs 12:25
Proverbs 12:25.content: Care, fear, and sorrow, upon the spirits, deprive men of vigour in what is to be done, or courage in what is to be borne. A good word from God, applied by faith, makes the heart glad.

Proverbs 12:26.title: Proverbs 12:26
Proverbs 12:26.content: The righteous is abundant; though not in this world's goods, yet in the graces and comforts of the Spirit, which are the true riches. Evil men vainly flatter themselves that their ways are not wrong.

Proverbs 12:27.title: Proverbs 12:27
Proverbs 12:27.content: The slothful man makes no good use of the advantages Providence puts in his way, and has no comfort in them. The substance of a diligent man, though not great, does good to him and his family. He sees that God gives it to him in answer to prayer.

Proverbs 12:28.title: Proverbs 12:28
Proverbs 12:28.content: The way of religion is a straight, plain way; it is the way of righteousness. There is not only life at the end, but life in the way; all true comfort. Proverbs

Proverbs 13:1.title: Proverbs 13:1
Proverbs 13:1.content: There is great hope of those that reverence their parents. There is little hope of any who will not hear those that deal faithfully with them.

Proverbs 13:2.title: Proverbs 13:2
Proverbs 13:2.content: By our words we must be justified or condemned, Matthew 12:37.

Proverbs 13:3.title: Proverbs 13:3
Proverbs 13:3.content: He that thinks before he speaks, that suppresses evil if he have thought it, keeps his soul from a great deal both of guilt and grief. Many a one is ruined by an ungoverned tongue.

Proverbs 13:4.title: Proverbs 13:4
Proverbs 13:4.content: The slothful desire the gains the diligent get, but hate the pains the diligent take; therefore they have nothing. This is especially true as to the soul.

Proverbs 13:5.title: Proverbs 13:5
Proverbs 13:5.content: Where sin reigns, the man is loathsome. If his conscience were awake, he would abhor himself, and repent in dust and ashes.

Proverbs 13:6.title: Proverbs 13:6
Proverbs 13:6.content: An honest desire to do right, preserves a man from fatal mistakes, better than a thousand fine-drawn distinctions.

Proverbs 13:7.title: Proverbs 13:7
Proverbs 13:7.content: Some who are really poor, trade and spend as if they were rich: this is sin, and will be shame, and it will end accordingly. Some that are really rich, would be thought to be poor: in this there is want of gratitude to God, want of justice and charity to others. There are many hypocrites, empty of grace, who will not be convinced of their poverty. There are many fearing Christians, who are spiritually rich, yet think themselves poor; by their doubts, and complaints, and griefs, they make themselves poor.

Proverbs 13:8.title: Proverbs 13:8
Proverbs 13:8.content: Great riches often tempt to violence against those that possess them; but the poor are free from such perils.

Proverbs 13:9.title: Proverbs 13:9
Proverbs 13:9.content: The light of the righteous is as that of the sun, which may be eclipsed and clouded, but will continue: the Spirit is their Light, he gives a fulness of joy: that of the wicked is as a lamp of their own kindling, easily put out.

Proverbs 13:10.title: Proverbs 13:10
Proverbs 13:10.content: All contentions, whether between private persons, families, churches, or nations, are begun and carried forward by pride. Disputes would be easily prevented or ended, if it were not for pride.

Proverbs 13:11.title: Proverbs 13:11
Proverbs 13:11.content: Wealth gotten by dishonesty or vice, has a secret curse, which will speedily waste it.

Proverbs 13:12.title: Proverbs 13:12
Proverbs 13:12.content: The delay of what is anxiously hoped for, is very painful to the mind; obtaining it is very pleasant. But spiritual blessings are chiefly intended.

Proverbs 13:13.title: Proverbs 13:13
Proverbs 13:13.content: He that stands in awe of God, and reverences his word, shall escape destruction, and be rewarded for his godly fear.

Proverbs 13:14.title: Proverbs 13:14
Proverbs 13:14.content: The rule by which the wise regulate their conduct, is a fountain yielding life and happiness.

Proverbs 13:15.title: Proverbs 13:15
Proverbs 13:15.content: The way of sinners is hard upon others, and hard to the sinner himself. The service of sin is slavery; the road to hell is strewed with the thorns and thistles that followed the curse.

Proverbs 13:16.title: Proverbs 13:16
Proverbs 13:16.content: It is folly to talk of things of which we know nothing, and to undertake what we are no way fit for.

Proverbs 13:17.title: Proverbs 13:17
Proverbs 13:17.content: Those that are wicked, and false to Christ and to the souls of men, do mischief, and fall into mischief; but those that are faithful, find sound words healing to others and to themselves.

Proverbs 13:18.title: Proverbs 13:18
Proverbs 13:18.content: He that scorns to be taught, will certainly be brought down.

Proverbs 13:19.title: Proverbs 13:19
Proverbs 13:19.content: There are in man strong desires after happiness; but never let those expect any thing truly sweet to their souls, who will not be persuaded to leave their sins.

Proverbs 13:20.title: Proverbs 13:20
Proverbs 13:20.content: Multitudes are brought to ruin by bad company. And all that make themselves wicked will be destroyed.

Proverbs 13:21.title: Proverbs 13:21
Proverbs 13:21.content: When God pursues sinners he is sure to overtake them; and he will reward the righteous.

Proverbs 13:22.title: Proverbs 13:22
Proverbs 13:22.content: The servant of God who is not anxious about riches, takes the best method of providing for his children.

Proverbs 13:23.title: Proverbs 13:23
Proverbs 13:23.content: The poor, yet industrious, thrive, though in a homely manner, while those who have great riches are often brought to poverty for want of judgment.

Proverbs 13:24.title: Proverbs 13:24
Proverbs 13:24.content: He acts as if he hated his child, who, by false indulgence, permits sinful habits to gather strength, which will bring sorrow here, and misery hereafter.

Proverbs 13:25.title: Proverbs 13:25
Proverbs 13:25.content: It is the misery of the wicked, that even their sensual appetites are always craving. The righteous feeds on the word and ordinances, to the satisfying of his soul with the promises of the gospel, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who is the Bread of life. Proverbs

Proverbs 14:1.title: Proverbs 14:1
Proverbs 14:1.content: A woman who has no fear of God, who is wilful and wasteful, and indulges her ease, will as certainly ruin her family, as if she plucked her house down.

Proverbs 14:2.title: Proverbs 14:2
Proverbs 14:2.content: Here are grace and sin in their true colours. Those that despise God's precepts and promises, despise God and all his power and mercy.

Proverbs 14:3.title: Proverbs 14:3
Proverbs 14:3.content: Pride grows from that root of bitterness which is in the heart. The root must be plucked up, or we cannot conquer this branch. The prudent words of wise men get them out of difficulties.

Proverbs 14:4.title: Proverbs 14:4
Proverbs 14:4.content: There can be no advantage without something which, though of little moment, will affright the indolent.

Proverbs 14:5.title: Proverbs 14:5
Proverbs 14:5.content: A conscientious witness will not dare to represent anything otherwise than according to his knowledge.

Proverbs 14:6.title: Proverbs 14:6
Proverbs 14:6.content: A scorner treats Divine things with contempt. He that feels his ignorance and unworthiness will search the Scriptures in a humble spirit.

Proverbs 14:7.title: Proverbs 14:7
Proverbs 14:7.content: We discover a wicked man if there is no savour of piety in his discourse.

Proverbs 14:8.title: Proverbs 14:8
Proverbs 14:8.content: We are travellers, whose concern is, not to spy out wonders, but to get to their journey's end; to understand the rules we are to walk by, also the ends we are to walk toward. The bad man cheats himself, and goes on in his mistake.

Proverbs 14:9.title: Proverbs 14:9
Proverbs 14:9.content: Foolish and profane men consider sin a mere trifle, to be made light of rather than mourned over. Fools mock at the sin-offering; but those that make light of sin, make light of Christ.

Proverbs 14:10.title: Proverbs 14:10
Proverbs 14:10.content: We do not know what stings of conscience, or consuming passions, torment the prosperous sinner. Nor does the world know the peace of mind a serious Christian enjoys, even in poverty and sickness.

Proverbs 14:11.title: Proverbs 14:11
Proverbs 14:11.content: Sin ruins many great families; whilst righteousness often raises and strengthens even mean families.

Proverbs 14:12.title: Proverbs 14:12
Proverbs 14:12.content: The ways of carelessness, of worldliness, and of sensuality, seem right to those that walk in them; but self-deceivers prove self-destroyers. See the vanity of carnal mirth.

Proverbs 14:14.title: Proverbs 14:14
Proverbs 14:14.content: Of all sinners backsliders will have the most terror when they reflect on their own ways.

Proverbs 14:15.title: Proverbs 14:15
Proverbs 14:15.content: Eager readiness to believe what others say, has ever proved mischievous. The whole world was thus ruined at first. The man who is spiritually wise, depends on the Saviour alone for acceptance. He is watchful against the enemies of his salvation, by taking heed to God's word.

Proverbs 14:16.title: Proverbs 14:16
Proverbs 14:16.content: Holy fear guards against every thing unholy.

Proverbs 14:17.title: Proverbs 14:17
Proverbs 14:17.content: An angry man is to be pitied as well as blamed; but the revengeful is more hateful.

Proverbs 14:18.title: Proverbs 14:18
Proverbs 14:18.content: Sin is the shame of sinners; but wisdom is the honour of the wise.

Proverbs 14:19.title: Proverbs 14:19
Proverbs 14:19.content: Even bad men acknowledge the excellency of God's people.

Proverbs 14:20.title: Proverbs 14:20
Proverbs 14:20.content: Friendship in the world is governed by self-interest. It is good to have God our Friend; he will not desert us.

Proverbs 14:21.title: Proverbs 14:21
Proverbs 14:21.content: To despise a man for his employment or appearance is a sin.

Proverbs 14:22.title: Proverbs 14:22
Proverbs 14:22.content: How wisely those consult their own interest, who not only do good, but devise it!

Proverbs 14:23.title: Proverbs 14:23
Proverbs 14:23.content: Labour of the head, or of the hand, will turn to some good account. But if men's religion runs all out in talk and noise, they will come to nothing.

Proverbs 14:24.title: Proverbs 14:24
Proverbs 14:24.content: The riches of men of wisdom and piety enlarge their usefulness.

Proverbs 14:25.title: Proverbs 14:25
Proverbs 14:25.content: An upright man will venture the displeasure of the greatest, to bring truth to light.

Proverbs 14:26.title: Proverbs 14:26, 27
Proverbs 14:26.content: Those who fear the Lord so as to obey and serve him, have a strong ground of confidence, and will be preserved. Let us seek to this Fountain of life, that we may escape the snares of death.

Proverbs 14:27.title: Proverbs 14:26, 27
Proverbs 14:27.content: Those who fear the Lord so as to obey and serve him, have a strong ground of confidence, and will be preserved. Let us seek to this Fountain of life, that we may escape the snares of death.

Proverbs 14:28.title: Proverbs 14:28
Proverbs 14:28.content: Let all that wish well to the kingdom of Christ, do what they can, that many may be added to his church.

Proverbs 14:29.title: Proverbs 14:29
Proverbs 14:29.content: A mild, patient man is one that learns of Christ, who is Wisdom itself. Unbridled passion is folly made known.

Proverbs 14:30.title: Proverbs 14:30
Proverbs 14:30.content: An upright, contented, and benevolent mind, tends to health.

Proverbs 14:31.title: Proverbs 14:31
Proverbs 14:31.content: To oppress the poor is to reproach our Creator.

Proverbs 14:32.title: Proverbs 14:32
Proverbs 14:32.content: The wicked man has his soul forced from him; he dies in his sins, under the guilt and power of them. But godly men, though they have pain and some dread of death, have the blessed hope, which God, who cannot lie, has given them.

Proverbs 14:33.title: Proverbs 14:33
Proverbs 14:33.content: Wisdom possesses the heart, and thus regulates the affections and tempers.

Proverbs 14:34.title: Proverbs 14:34
Proverbs 14:34.content: Piety and holiness always promote industry, sobriety, and honesty.

Proverbs 14:35.title: Proverbs 14:35
Proverbs 14:35.content: The great King who reigns over heaven and earth, will reward faithful servants who honour his gospel by the proper discharge of the duties of their stations: he despises not the services of the lowest. Proverbs

Proverbs 15:1.title: Proverbs 15:1
Proverbs 15:1.content: A right cause will be better pleaded with meekness than with passion. Nothing stirs up anger like grievous words.

Proverbs 15:2.title: Proverbs 15:2
Proverbs 15:2.content: He that has knowledge, is to use it aright, for the good of others.

Proverbs 15:3.title: Proverbs 15:3
Proverbs 15:3.content: Secret sins, services, and sorrows, are under God's eye. This speaks comfort to saints, and terror to sinners.

Proverbs 15:4.title: Proverbs 15:4
Proverbs 15:4.content: A good tongue is healing to wounded consciences, by comforting them; to sin-sick souls, by convincing them; and it reconciles parties at variance.

Proverbs 15:5.title: Proverbs 15:5
Proverbs 15:5.content: If instruction is despised, reprove men rather than suffer them to go on undisturbed in the way to ruin.

Proverbs 15:6.title: Proverbs 15:6
Proverbs 15:6.content: The wealth of worldly men increases their fears and suspicions, adds strength to their passions, and renders the fear of death more distressing.

Proverbs 15:7.title: Proverbs 15:7
Proverbs 15:7.content: We use knowledge aright when we disperse it; but the heart of the foolish has nothing to disperse that is good.

Proverbs 15:8.title: Proverbs 15:8, 9
Proverbs 15:8.content: The wicked put other things in the stead of Christ's atonement, or in the place of holy obedience. Praying graces are his gift, and the work of his Spirit, with which he is well pleased.

Proverbs 15:9.title: Proverbs 15:8, 9
Proverbs 15:9.content: The wicked put other things in the stead of Christ's atonement, or in the place of holy obedience. Praying graces are his gift, and the work of his Spirit, with which he is well pleased.

Proverbs 15:10.title: Proverbs 15:10
Proverbs 15:10.content: He that hates reproof shall perish in his sins, since he would not be parted from them.

Proverbs 15:11.title: Proverbs 15:11
Proverbs 15:11.content: There is nothing that can be hid from the eyes of God, not even man's thoughts.

Proverbs 15:12.title: Proverbs 15:12
Proverbs 15:12.content: A scorner cannot bear to reflect seriously within his own heart.

Proverbs 15:13.title: Proverbs 15:13
Proverbs 15:13.content: A gloomy, impatient, unthankful spirit, springing from pride and undue attachment to worldly objects, renders a man uneasy to himself and others.

Proverbs 15:14.title: Proverbs 15:14
Proverbs 15:14.content: A wise man seeks to gain more wisdom, growing in grace and in the knowledge of Christ. But a carnal mind rests contented, flattering itself.

Proverbs 15:15.title: Proverbs 15:15
Proverbs 15:15.content: Some are much in affliction, and of a sorrowful spirit. Such are to be pitied, prayed for, and comforted. And others serve God with gladness of heart, and it prompts their obedience, yet they should rejoice with trembling.

Proverbs 15:16.title: Proverbs 15:16, 17
Proverbs 15:16.content: Believers often have enough when worldly eyes see little; the Lord is with them, without the cares, troubles, and temptations which are with the wealth of the wicked.

Proverbs 15:17.title: Proverbs 15:16, 17
Proverbs 15:17.content: Believers often have enough when worldly eyes see little; the Lord is with them, without the cares, troubles, and temptations which are with the wealth of the wicked.

Proverbs 15:18.title: Proverbs 15:18
Proverbs 15:18.content: He that is slow to anger, not only prevents strife, but appeases it, if kindled.

Proverbs 15:19.title: Proverbs 15:19
Proverbs 15:19.content: Those who have no heart to their work, pretend that they cannot do their work without hardship and danger. And thus many live always in doubt about their state, because always in neglect of some duty.

Proverbs 15:20.title: Proverbs 15:20
Proverbs 15:20.content: Those who treat an aged mother or a father with contempt or neglect, show their own folly.

Proverbs 15:21.title: Proverbs 15:21
Proverbs 15:21.content: Such as are truly wise, study that their thoughts, words, and actions should be regular, sincere, and holy.

Proverbs 15:22.title: Proverbs 15:22
Proverbs 15:22.content: If men will not take time and pains to deliberate, they are not likely to bring any thing to pass.

Proverbs 15:23.title: Proverbs 15:23
Proverbs 15:23.content: Wisdom is needed to suit our discourse to the occasions.

Proverbs 15:24.title: Proverbs 15:24
Proverbs 15:24.content: A good man sets his affections on things above; his way leads directly thither.

Proverbs 15:25.title: Proverbs 15:25
Proverbs 15:25.content: Pride is the ruin of multitudes. But those who are in affliction God will support.

Proverbs 15:26.title: Proverbs 15:26
Proverbs 15:26.content: The thoughts of wicked men offend Him who knows the heart.

Proverbs 15:27.title: Proverbs 15:27
Proverbs 15:27.content: The covetous man lets none of his family have rest or enjoyment. And greediness of gain often tempts to projects that bring ruin.

Proverbs 15:28.title: Proverbs 15:28
Proverbs 15:28.content: A good man is proved to be a wise man by this; he governs his tongue well.

Proverbs 15:29.title: Proverbs 15:29
Proverbs 15:29.content: God sets himself at a distance from those who set him at defiance.

Proverbs 15:30.title: Proverbs 15:30
Proverbs 15:30.content: How delightful to the humbled soul to hear the good report of salvation by the Lord Jesus Christ!

Proverbs 15:31.title: Proverbs 15:31
Proverbs 15:31.content: Faithful, friendly reproofs help spiritual life, and lead to eternal life.

Proverbs 15:32.title: Proverbs 15:32
Proverbs 15:32.content: Sinners undervalue their own souls; therefore they prefer the body before the soul, and wrong the soul to please the body.

Proverbs 15:33.title: Proverbs 15:33
Proverbs 15:33.content: The fear of the Lord will dispose us to search the Scriptures with reverence; and it will cause us to follow the leadings of the Holy Spirit. While we humbly place all our dependence on the grace of God, we are exalted in the righteousness of Christ. Proverbs

Proverbs 16:1.title: Proverbs 16:1
Proverbs 16:1.content: The renewing grace of God alone prepares the heart for every good work. This teaches us that we are not sufficient of ourselves to think or speak any thing wise and good.

Proverbs 16:2.title: Proverbs 16:2
Proverbs 16:2.content: Ignorance, pride, and self-flattery render us partial judges respecting our own conduct.

Proverbs 16:3.title: Proverbs 16:3
Proverbs 16:3.content: Roll the burden of thy care upon God, and leave it with him, by faith and dependence on him.

Proverbs 16:4.title: Proverbs 16:4
Proverbs 16:4.content: God makes use of the wicked to execute righteous vengeance on each other; and he will be glorified by their destruction at last.

Proverbs 16:5.title: Proverbs 16:5
Proverbs 16:5.content: Though sinners strengthen themselves and one another, they shall not escape God's judgments.

Proverbs 16:6.title: Proverbs 16:6
Proverbs 16:6.content: By the mercy and truth of God in Christ Jesus, the sins of believers are taken away, and the power of sin is broken.

Proverbs 16:7.title: Proverbs 16:7
Proverbs 16:7.content: He that has all hearts in his hand, can make a man's enemies to be at peace with him.

Proverbs 16:8.title: Proverbs 16:8
Proverbs 16:8.content: A small estate, honestly come by, will turn to better account than a great estate ill-gotten.

Proverbs 16:9.title: Proverbs 16:9
Proverbs 16:9.content: If men make God's glory their end, and his will their rule, he will direct their steps by his Spirit and grace. 10. Let kings and judges of the earth be just, and rule in the fear of God.

Proverbs 16:11.title: Proverbs 16:11
Proverbs 16:11.content: To observe justice in dealings between man and man is God's appointment.

Proverbs 16:12.title: Proverbs 16:12
Proverbs 16:12.content: The ruler that uses his power aright, will find that to be his best security.

Proverbs 16:13.title: Proverbs 16:13
Proverbs 16:13.content: Put those in power who know how to speak to the purpose.

Proverbs 16:14.title: Proverbs 16:14, 15
Proverbs 16:14.content: Those are fools, who, to obtain the favour of an earthly prince, throw themselves out of God's favour.

Proverbs 16:15.title: Proverbs 16:14, 15
Proverbs 16:15.content: Those are fools, who, to obtain the favour of an earthly prince, throw themselves out of God's favour.

Proverbs 16:16.title: Proverbs 16:16
Proverbs 16:16.content: There is joy and satisfaction of spirit, only in getting wisdom.

Proverbs 16:17.title: Proverbs 16:17
Proverbs 16:17.content: A sincerely religious man keeps at a distance from every appearance of evil. Happy is the man that walks in Christ, and is led by the Spirit of Christ.

Proverbs 16:18.title: Proverbs 16:18
Proverbs 16:18.content: When men defy God's judgments, and think themselves far from them, it is a sign they are at the door. Let us not fear the pride of others, but fear pride in ourselves.

Proverbs 16:19.title: Proverbs 16:19
Proverbs 16:19.content: Humility, though it exposes to contempt in the world, is much better than high-spiritedness, which makes God an enemy. He that understands God's word shall find good.

Proverbs 16:21.title: Proverbs 16:21
Proverbs 16:21.content: The man whose wisdom dwells in his heart, will be found more truly prudent than many who possess shining talents.

Proverbs 16:22.title: Proverbs 16:22
Proverbs 16:22.content: As waters to a thirsty land, so is a wise man to his friends and neighbours.

Proverbs 16:23.title: Proverbs 16:23
Proverbs 16:23.content: The wise man's self-knowledge, always suggests something proper to be spoken to others.

Proverbs 16:24.title: Proverbs 16:24
Proverbs 16:24.content: The word of God cures the diseases that weaken our souls.

Proverbs 16:25.title: Proverbs 16:25
Proverbs 16:25.content: This is caution to all, to take heed of deceiving themselves as to their souls.

Proverbs 16:26.title: Proverbs 16:26
Proverbs 16:26.content: We must labour for the meat which endureth to everlasting life, or we must perish.

Proverbs 16:27.title: Proverbs 16:27, 28
Proverbs 16:27.content: Ungodly men bestow more pains to do mischief than would be needful to do good. The whisperer separates friends: what a hateful, but how common a character!

Proverbs 16:28.title: Proverbs 16:27, 28
Proverbs 16:28.content: Ungodly men bestow more pains to do mischief than would be needful to do good. The whisperer separates friends: what a hateful, but how common a character!

Proverbs 16:29.title: Proverbs 16:29, 30
Proverbs 16:29.content: Some do all the mischief they can by force and violence, and are blind to the result.

Proverbs 16:30.title: Proverbs 16:29, 30
Proverbs 16:30.content: Some do all the mischief they can by force and violence, and are blind to the result.

Proverbs 16:31.title: Proverbs 16:31
Proverbs 16:31.content: Old people especially should be found in the way of religion and godliness.

Proverbs 16:32.title: Proverbs 16:32
Proverbs 16:32.content: To overcome our own passions, requires more steady management, than obtaining victory over an enemy.

Proverbs 16:33.title: Proverbs 16:33
Proverbs 16:33.content: All the disposal of Providence concerning our affairs, we must look upon to be the determining what we referred to God; and we must be reconciled to them accordingly. Blessed are those that give themselves up to the will of God; for he knows what is good for them. Proverbs

Proverbs 17:1.title: Proverbs 17:1
Proverbs 17:1.content: These words recommend family love and peace, as needful for the comfort of human life.

Proverbs 17:2.title: Proverbs 17:2
Proverbs 17:2.content: The wise servant is more deserving, and more likely to appear one of the family, than a profligate son.

Proverbs 17:3.title: Proverbs 17:3
Proverbs 17:3.content: God tries the heart by affliction. He thus has often shown the sin remaining in the heart of the believer.

Proverbs 17:4.title: Proverbs 17:4
Proverbs 17:4.content: Flatterers, especially false teachers, are welcome to those that live in sin.

Proverbs 17:5.title: Proverbs 17:5
Proverbs 17:5.content: Those that laugh at poverty, treat God's providence and precepts with contempt.

Proverbs 17:6.title: Proverbs 17:6
Proverbs 17:6.content: It is an honour to children to have wise and godly parents continued to them, even after they are grown up and settled in the world.

Proverbs 17:7.title: Proverbs 17:7
Proverbs 17:7.content: A fool, in Solomon's Proverbs, signifies a wicked man, whom excellent speech does not become, because his conversation contradicts it.

Proverbs 17:8.title: Proverbs 17:8
Proverbs 17:8.content: Those who set their hearts upon money, will do any thing for it. What influence should the gifts of God have on our hearts!

Proverbs 17:9.title: Proverbs 17:9
Proverbs 17:9.content: The way to preserve peace is to make the best of every thing; not to notice what has been said or done against ourselves.

Proverbs 17:10.title: Proverbs 17:10
Proverbs 17:10.content: A gentle reproof will enter, not only into the head, but into the heart of a wise man.

Proverbs 17:11.title: Proverbs 17:11
Proverbs 17:11.content: Satan, and the messengers of Satan, shall be let loose upon an evil man.

Proverbs 17:12.title: Proverbs 17:12
Proverbs 17:12.content: Let us watch over our own passions, and avoid the company of furious men.

Proverbs 17:13.title: Proverbs 17:13
Proverbs 17:13.content: To render evil for good is devilish. He that does so, brings a curse upon his family.

Proverbs 17:14.title: Proverbs 17:14
Proverbs 17:14.content: What danger there is in the beginning of strife! Resist its earliest display; and leave it off, if it were possible, before you begin.

Proverbs 17:15.title: Proverbs 17:15
Proverbs 17:15.content: It is an offence to God to acquit the guilty, or to condemn those who are not guilty.

Proverbs 17:16.title: Proverbs 17:16
Proverbs 17:16.content: Man's neglect of God's favour and his own interest is very absurd.

Proverbs 17:17.title: Proverbs 17:17
Proverbs 17:17.content: No change of outward circumstances should abate our affection for our friends or relatives. But no friend, except Christ, deserves unlimited confidence. In Him this text did receive, and still receives its most glorious fulfilment.

Proverbs 17:18.title: Proverbs 17:18
Proverbs 17:18.content: Let not any wrong their families. Yet Christ's becoming Surety for men, was a glorious display of Divine wisdom; for he was able to discharge the bond.

Proverbs 17:19.title: Proverbs 17:19
Proverbs 17:19.content: If we would keep a clear conscience and a quiet mind, we must shun all excitements to anger. And a man who affects a style of living above his means, goes the way to ruin.

Proverbs 17:20.title: Proverbs 17:20
Proverbs 17:20.content: There is nothing got by ill designs. And many have paid dear for an unbridled tongue.

Proverbs 17:21.title: Proverbs 17:21
Proverbs 17:21.content: This speaks very plainly what many wise and good men feel very strongly, how grievous it is to have a foolish, wicked child.

Proverbs 17:22.title: Proverbs 17:22
Proverbs 17:22.content: It is great mercy that God gives us leave to be cheerful, and cause to be cheerful, if by his grace he gives us hearts to be cheerful.

Proverbs 17:23.title: Proverbs 17:23
Proverbs 17:23.content: The wicked are ready to part with their money, though loved, that they may not suffer for their crimes.

Proverbs 17:24.title: Proverbs 17:24
Proverbs 17:24.content: The prudent man keeps the word of God continually in view. But the foolish man cannot fix his thoughts, nor pursue any purpose with steadiness.

Proverbs 17:25.title: Proverbs 17:25
Proverbs 17:25.content: Wicked children despise the authority of their father, and the tenderness of their mother.

Proverbs 17:26.title: Proverbs 17:26
Proverbs 17:26.content: It is very wrong to find fault for doing what is duty.

Proverbs 17:27.title: Proverbs 17:27, 28
Proverbs 17:27.content: A man may show himself to be a wise man, by the good temper of his mind, and by the good government of his tongue. He is careful when he does speak, to speak to the purpose. God knows his heart, and the folly that is bound there; therefore he cannot be deceived in his judgment as men may be. Proverbs

Proverbs 17:28.title: Proverbs 17:27, 28
Proverbs 17:28.content: A man may show himself to be a wise man, by the good temper of his mind, and by the good government of his tongue. He is careful when he does speak, to speak to the purpose. God knows his heart, and the folly that is bound there; therefore he cannot be deceived in his judgment as men may be. Proverbs

Proverbs 18:1.title: Proverbs 18:1
Proverbs 18:1.content: If we would get knowledge and grace, we must try all methods of improving ourselves.

Proverbs 18:2.title: Proverbs 18:2
Proverbs 18:2.content: Those make nothing to purpose, of learning or religion, whose only design is to have something to make a show with.

Proverbs 18:3.title: Proverbs 18:3
Proverbs 18:3.content: As soon as sin entered, shame followed.

Proverbs 18:4.title: Proverbs 18:4
Proverbs 18:4.content: The well-spring of wisdom in the heart of a believer, continually supplies words of wisdom.

Proverbs 18:5.title: Proverbs 18:5
Proverbs 18:5.content: The merits of a cause must be looked to, not the person.

Proverbs 18:6.title: Proverbs 18:6, 7
Proverbs 18:6.content: What mischief bad men do to themselves by their ungoverned tongues!

Proverbs 18:7.title: Proverbs 18:6, 7
Proverbs 18:7.content: What mischief bad men do to themselves by their ungoverned tongues!

Proverbs 18:8.title: Proverbs 18:8
Proverbs 18:8.content: How base are those that sow contention! and what fatal effects may be expected from small beginnings of jealousy!

Proverbs 18:9.title: Proverbs 18:9
Proverbs 18:9.content: Omissions of duty, and in duty, are fatal to the soul, as well as commissions of sin.

Proverbs 18:10.title: Proverbs 18:10, 11
Proverbs 18:10.content: The Divine power, made known in and through our Lord Jesus Christ, forms a strong tower for the believer, who relies on the Lord. How deceitful the defence of the rich man, who has his portion and treasure in this world! It is a strong city and a high wall only in his own conceit; for it will fail when most in need. They will be exposed to the just wrath of that Judge whom they despised as a Saviour.

Proverbs 18:11.title: Proverbs 18:10, 11
Proverbs 18:11.content: The Divine power, made known in and through our Lord Jesus Christ, forms a strong tower for the believer, who relies on the Lord. How deceitful the defence of the rich man, who has his portion and treasure in this world! It is a strong city and a high wall only in his own conceit; for it will fail when most in need. They will be exposed to the just wrath of that Judge whom they despised as a Saviour.

Proverbs 18:12.title: Proverbs 18:12
Proverbs 18:12.content: After the heart has been lifted up with pride, a fall comes. But honour shall be the reward of humility.

Proverbs 18:13.title: Proverbs 18:13
Proverbs 18:13.content: Eagerness, with self-conceit, will expose to shame.

Proverbs 18:14.title: Proverbs 18:14
Proverbs 18:14.content: Firmness of mind supports under many pains and trials. But when the conscience is tortured with remorse, no human fortitude can bear the misery; what then will hell be?

Proverbs 18:15.title: Proverbs 18:15
Proverbs 18:15.content: We must get knowledge, not only into our heads, but into our hearts.

Proverbs 18:16.title: Proverbs 18:16
Proverbs 18:16.content: Blessed be the Lord, who makes us welcome to come to his throne, without money and without price. May his gifts make room for him in our souls.

Proverbs 18:17.title: Proverbs 18:17
Proverbs 18:17.content: It is well to listen to our enemies, that we may form a better judgment of ourselves.

Proverbs 18:18.title: Proverbs 18:18
Proverbs 18:18.content: It was customary sometimes to refer matters to God, by casting lots, with solemn prayer. The profaning the lot, by using it in matters of diversion, or coveting what belongs to others, forms an objection to this now.

Proverbs 18:19.title: Proverbs 18:19
Proverbs 18:19.content: Great care must be taken to prevent quarrels among relations and those under obligations to each other. Wisdom and grace make it easy to forgive; but corruption makes it difficult.

Proverbs 18:20.title: Proverbs 18:20
Proverbs 18:20.content: The belly is here put for the heart, as elsewhere; and what that is filled with, our satisfaction will be accordingly, and our inward peace.

Proverbs 18:21.title: Proverbs 18:21
Proverbs 18:21.content: Many a one has caused his own death, or the death of others, by a false or injurious tongue.

Proverbs 18:22.title: Proverbs 18:22
Proverbs 18:22.content: A good wife is a great blessing to a man, and it is a token of Divine favour.

Proverbs 18:23.title: Proverbs 18:23
Proverbs 18:23.content: Poverty tells men they must not order or demand. And at the throne of God's grace we are all poor, and must use entreaties.

Proverbs 18:24.title: Proverbs 18:24
Proverbs 18:24.content: Christ Jesus never will forsake those who trust in and love him. May we be such friends to others, for our Master's sake. Having loved his own, which were in the world, he loved them unto the end; and we are his friends if we do whatever he commands us, John 15:14. Proverbs

Proverbs 19:1.title: Proverbs 19:1
Proverbs 19:1.content: A poor man who fears God, is more honourable and happy, than a man without wisdom and grace, however rich or advanced in rank.

Proverbs 19:2.title: Proverbs 19:2
Proverbs 19:2.content: What good can the soul do, if without knowledge? And he sins who will not take time to ponder the path of his feet.

Proverbs 19:3.title: Proverbs 19:3
Proverbs 19:3.content: Men run into troubles by their own folly, and then fret at the appointments of God.

Proverbs 19:4.title: Proverbs 19:4
Proverbs 19:4.content: Here we may see how strong is men's love of money.

Proverbs 19:5.title: Proverbs 19:5
Proverbs 19:5.content: Those that tell lies in discourse, are in a fair way to be guilty of bearing false-witness.

Proverbs 19:6.title: Proverbs 19:6
Proverbs 19:6.content: We are without excuse if we do not love God with all our hearts. His gifts to us are past number, and all the gifts of men to us are fruits of his bounty.

Proverbs 19:7.title: Proverbs 19:7
Proverbs 19:7.content: Christ was left by all his disciples; but the Father was with him. It encourages our faith that he had so large an experience of the sorrows of poverty.

Proverbs 19:8.title: Proverbs 19:8
Proverbs 19:8.content: Those only love their souls aright that get true wisdom.

Proverbs 19:9.title: Proverbs 19:9
Proverbs 19:9.content: Lying is a damning, destroying sin.

Proverbs 19:10.title: Proverbs 19:10
Proverbs 19:10.content: A man that has not wisdom and grace, has no right or title to true joy. It is very unseemly for one who is a servant to sin, to oppress God's free-men.

Proverbs 19:11.title: Proverbs 19:11
Proverbs 19:11.content: He attains the most true glory who endeavours most steadily to overcome evil with good.

Proverbs 19:12.title: Proverbs 19:12
Proverbs 19:12.content: Christ is a King, whose wrath against his enemies will be as the roaring of a lion, and his favour to his people as the refreshing dew.

Proverbs 19:13.title: Proverbs 19:13
Proverbs 19:13.content: It shows the vanity of the world, that we are liable to the greatest griefs where we promise ourselves the greatest comfort.

Proverbs 19:14.title: Proverbs 19:14
Proverbs 19:14.content: A discreet and virtuous wife is more valuable than house and riches.

Proverbs 19:15.title: Proverbs 19:15
Proverbs 19:15.content: A sluggish, slothful disposition makes men poor; it brings them to want. And this applies both to the present life and that which is to come.

Proverbs 19:16.title: Proverbs 19:16
Proverbs 19:16.content: If we keep God's word, God's word will keep us from every thing really hurtful. We abuse the doctrine of free grace, if we think that it does away the necessity and advantage of obedience. Those that live at random must die. This truth is clearly taught in words enough to alarm the stoutest sinner.

Proverbs 19:17.title: Proverbs 19:17
Proverbs 19:17.content: God has chosen the poor of this world, to be rich in faith, and heirs of his kingdom.

Proverbs 19:18.title: Proverbs 19:18
Proverbs 19:18.content: When parents keep under foolish tenderness, they do their best to render children a comfort to them, and happy in themselves.

Proverbs 19:19.title: Proverbs 19:19
Proverbs 19:19.content: The spared and spoiled child is likely to become a man of great wrath.

Proverbs 19:20.title: Proverbs 19:20
Proverbs 19:20.content: Those that would be wise in their latter end, must be taught and ruled when young.

Proverbs 19:21.title: Proverbs 19:21
Proverbs 19:21.content: What should we desire, but that all our purposes may agree with God's holy will?

Proverbs 19:22.title: Proverbs 19:22
Proverbs 19:22.content: It is far better to have a heart to do good, and want ability for it, than to have ability for it, and want a heart to it.

Proverbs 19:23.title: Proverbs 19:23
Proverbs 19:23.content: Those that live in the fear of God, shall get safety, satisfaction, and true and complete happiness.

Proverbs 19:24.title: Proverbs 19:24
Proverbs 19:24.content: Indolence, when indulged, so grows upon people, that they have no heart to do the most needful things for themselves.

Proverbs 19:25.title: Proverbs 19:25
Proverbs 19:25.content: A gentle rebuke goes farthest with a man of understanding.

Proverbs 19:26.title: Proverbs 19:26
Proverbs 19:26.content: The young man who wastes his father's substance, or makes his aged mother destitute, is hateful, and will come to disgrace.

Proverbs 19:27.title: Proverbs 19:27
Proverbs 19:27.content: It is the wisdom of young men to dread hearing such talk as puts loose and evil principles into the mind.

Proverbs 19:28.title: Proverbs 19:28
Proverbs 19:28.content: Those are the worst of sinners, who are glad of an opportunity to sin.

Proverbs 19:29.title: Proverbs 19:29
Proverbs 19:29.content: The unbelief of man shall not make God's threatenings of no effect. Christ himself, when bearing sins not his own, was not spared. Justice and judgment took hold of our blessed Surety; and will God spare obstinate sinners? Proverbs

Proverbs 20:1.title: Proverbs 20:1
Proverbs 20:1.content: It seems hard to believe that men of the greatest abilities, as well as the ignorant, should render themselves fools and madmen, merely for the taste or excitement produced by strong liquors.

Proverbs 20:2.title: Proverbs 20:2
Proverbs 20:2.content: How formidable kings are to those who provoke them! how much more foolish then is it to provoke the King of kings!

Proverbs 20:3.title: Proverbs 20:3
Proverbs 20:3.content: To engage in quarrels is the greatest folly that can be. Yield, and even give up just demands, for peace' sake.

Proverbs 20:4.title: Proverbs 20:4
Proverbs 20:4.content: He who labours and endures hardship in his seed- time for eternity, will be properly diligent as to his earthly business.

Proverbs 20:5.title: Proverbs 20:5
Proverbs 20:5.content: Though many capable of giving wise counsel are silent, yet something may be drawn from them, which will reward those who obtain it.

Proverbs 20:6.title: Proverbs 20:6
Proverbs 20:6.content: It is hard to find those that have done, and will do more good than they speak, or care to hear spoken of.

Proverbs 20:7.title: Proverbs 20:7
Proverbs 20:7.content: A good man is not liable to uneasiness in contriving what he shall do, or in reflecting on what he has done, as those who walk in deceit. And his family fare better for his sake.

Proverbs 20:8.title: Proverbs 20:8
Proverbs 20:8.content: If great men are good men, they may do much good, and prevent very much evil.

Proverbs 20:9.title: Proverbs 20:9
Proverbs 20:9.content: Some can say, Through grace, we are cleaner than we have been; but it was the work of the Holy Spirit.

Proverbs 20:10.title: Proverbs 20:10
Proverbs 20:10.content: See the various deceits men use, of which the love of money is the root. The Lord will not bless what is thus gotten.

Proverbs 20:11.title: Proverbs 20:11
Proverbs 20:11.content: Parents should observe their children, that they may manage them accordingly.

Proverbs 20:12.title: Proverbs 20:12
Proverbs 20:12.content: All our powers and faculties are from God, and are to be employed for him.

Proverbs 20:13.title: Proverbs 20:13
Proverbs 20:13.content: Those that indulge themselves, may expect to want necessaries, which should have been gotten by honest labour.

Proverbs 20:14.title: Proverbs 20:14
Proverbs 20:14.content: Men use arts to get a good bargain, and to buy cheap; whereas a man ought to be ashamed of a fraud and a lie.

Proverbs 20:15.title: Proverbs 20:15
Proverbs 20:15.content: He that prefers true knowledge to riches, follows the ways of religion and happiness. If we really believed this truth, the word of God would be valued as it deserves, and the world would lose its tempting influence. Proverbs 20:16. Those ruin themselves who entangle themselves in rash suretyship. Also those who are in league with abandoned women. Place no confidence in either.

Proverbs 20:17.title: Proverbs 20:17
Proverbs 20:17.content: Wealth gotten by fraud may be sweet, for the carnal mind takes pleasure in the success of wicked devices; but it will be bitter in the reflection.

Proverbs 20:18.title: Proverbs 20:18
Proverbs 20:18.content: Especially we need advice in spiritual warfare. The word and Spirit of God are the best counsellors in every point.

Proverbs 20:19.title: Proverbs 20:19
Proverbs 20:19.content: Those dearly buy their own praise, who put confidence in a man because he speaks fairly.

Proverbs 20:20.title: Proverbs 20:20
Proverbs 20:20.content: An undutiful child will become very miserable. Never let him expect any peace or comfort.

Proverbs 20:21.title: Proverbs 20:21
Proverbs 20:21.content: An estate suddenly raised, is often as suddenly ruined.

Proverbs 20:22.title: Proverbs 20:22
Proverbs 20:22.content: Wait on the Lord, attend his pleasure, and he will protect thee.

Proverbs 20:23.title: Proverbs 20:23
Proverbs 20:23.content: A bargain made by fraud will prove a losing bargain in the end.

Proverbs 20:24.title: Proverbs 20:24
Proverbs 20:24.content: How can we form plans, and conduct business, independently of the Lord?

Proverbs 20:25.title: Proverbs 20:25
Proverbs 20:25.content: The evasions men often use with their own consciences show how false and deceitful man is.

Proverbs 20:26.title: Proverbs 20:26
Proverbs 20:26.content: Justice should crush the wicked, and separate them from the virtuous.

Proverbs 20:27.title: Proverbs 20:27
Proverbs 20:27.content: The rational soul and conscience are as a lamp within us, which should be used in examining our dispositions and motives with the revealed will of God.

Proverbs 20:28.title: Proverbs 20:28
Proverbs 20:28.content: Mercy and truth are the glories of God's throne.

Proverbs 20:29.title: Proverbs 20:29
Proverbs 20:29.content: Both young and old have their advantages; and let neither despise or envy the other.

Proverbs 20:30.title: Proverbs 20:30
Proverbs 20:30.content: Severe rebukes sometimes do a great deal of good. But such is the corruption of nature, that men are loth to be rebuked for their sins. If God uses severe afflictions, to purify our hearts and fit us for his service, we have cause to be very thankful. Proverbs

Proverbs 21:1.title: Proverbs 21:1
Proverbs 21:1.content: The believer, perceiving that the Lord rules every heart as he sees fit, like the husbandman who turns the water through his grounds as he pleases, seeks to have his own heart, and the hearts of others, directed in his faith, fear, and love.

Proverbs 21:2.title: Proverbs 21:2
Proverbs 21:2.content: We are partial in judging ourselves and our actions.

Proverbs 21:3.title: Proverbs 21:3
Proverbs 21:3.content: Many deceive themselves with a conceit that outward devotions will excuse unrighteousness.

Proverbs 21:4.title: Proverbs 21:4
Proverbs 21:4.content: Sin is the pride, the ambition, the glory, the joy, and the business of wicked men.

Proverbs 21:5.title: Proverbs 21:5
Proverbs 21:5.content: The really diligent employ foresight as well as labour.

Proverbs 21:6.title: Proverbs 21:6
Proverbs 21:6.content: While men seek wealth by unlawful practices, they seek death.

Proverbs 21:7.title: Proverbs 21:7
Proverbs 21:7.content: Injustice will return upon the sinner, and will destroy him here and for ever.

Proverbs 21:8.title: Proverbs 21:8
Proverbs 21:8.content: The way of mankind by nature is froward and strange.

Proverbs 21:9.title: Proverbs 21:9
Proverbs 21:9.content: It is best to shun bitter contention by pouring out the heart before God. For by prudence and patience, with constant prayer, the cross may be removed.

Proverbs 21:10.title: Proverbs 21:10
Proverbs 21:10.content: The evil desires of a wicked man's heart, lead to baseness in his conduct.

Proverbs 21:11.title: Proverbs 21:11
Proverbs 21:11.content: The simple may be made wise by punishments on the wicked, and by instructions to those who are willing to be taught.

Proverbs 21:12.title: Proverbs 21:12
Proverbs 21:12.content: Good men envy not the prosperity of evil-doers; they see there is a curse on them.

Proverbs 21:13.title: Proverbs 21:13
Proverbs 21:13.content: Such as oppress the poor by beating down wages, such as will not relieve according to their ability those in distress, and those in authority who neglect to do justice, stop their ears at the cry of the poor. But doubtless care is to be used in the exercise of charity.

Proverbs 21:14.title: Proverbs 21:14
Proverbs 21:14.content: If money can conquer the fury of the passions, shall reason, the fear of God, and the command of Christ, be too weak to bridle them?

Proverbs 21:15.title: Proverbs 21:15
Proverbs 21:15.content: There is true pleasure only in the practice of religion.

Proverbs 21:16.title: Proverbs 21:16
Proverbs 21:16.content: Of all wanderers in the ways of sin, those are in the most dangerous condition who turn aside into the ways of darkness. Yet there is hope even for them in the all-sufficient Saviour; but let them flee to him without delay.

Proverbs 21:17.title: Proverbs 21:17
Proverbs 21:17.content: A life of worldly pleasure brings ruin on men.

Proverbs 21:18.title: Proverbs 21:18
Proverbs 21:18.content: The righteous is often delivered out of trouble, and the wicked comes in his stead, and so seems as a ransom for him.

Proverbs 21:19.title: Proverbs 21:19
Proverbs 21:19.content: Unbridled passions spoil the comfort of all relations.

Proverbs 21:20.title: Proverbs 21:20
Proverbs 21:20.content: The plenty obtained by prudence, industry, and frugality, is desirable. But the foolish misspend what they have upon their lusts.

Proverbs 21:21.title: Proverbs 21:21
Proverbs 21:21.content: True repentance and faith will lead him that relies on the mercy of God in Christ, to follow after righteousness and mercy in his own conduct.

Proverbs 21:22.title: Proverbs 21:22
Proverbs 21:22.content: Those that have wisdom, often do great things, even against those confident of their strength.

Proverbs 21:23.title: Proverbs 21:23
Proverbs 21:23.content: It is our great concern to keep our souls from being entangled and disquieted.

Proverbs 21:24.title: Proverbs 21:24
Proverbs 21:24.content: Pride and haughtiness make men passionate; such continually deal in wrath, as if it were their trade to be angry.

Proverbs 21:25.title: Proverbs 21:25, 26
Proverbs 21:25.content: Here is the misery of the slothful; their hands refuse to labour in an honest calling, by which they might get an honest livelihood; yet their hearts cease not to covet riches, pleasures, and honours, which cannot be obtained without labour. But the righteous and industrious have their desires satisfied.

Proverbs 21:26.title: Proverbs 21:25, 26
Proverbs 21:26.content: Here is the misery of the slothful; their hands refuse to labour in an honest calling, by which they might get an honest livelihood; yet their hearts cease not to covet riches, pleasures, and honours, which cannot be obtained without labour. But the righteous and industrious have their desires satisfied.

Proverbs 21:27.title: Proverbs 21:27
Proverbs 21:27.content: When holiness is pretended, but wickedness intended, that especially is an abomination.

Proverbs 21:28.title: Proverbs 21:28
Proverbs 21:28.content: The doom of a false witness is certain.

Proverbs 21:29.title: Proverbs 21:29
Proverbs 21:29.content: A wicked man bids defiance to the terrors of the law and the rebukes of Providence. But a good man asks, What does God require of me?

Proverbs 21:30.title: Proverbs 21:30, 31
Proverbs 21:30.content: Means are to be used, but, after all, our safety and salvation are only of the Lord. In our spiritual warfare we must arm ourselves with the whole armour of God; but our strength must be in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Proverbs

Proverbs 21:31.title: Proverbs 21:30, 31
Proverbs 21:31.content: Means are to be used, but, after all, our safety and salvation are only of the Lord. In our spiritual warfare we must arm ourselves with the whole armour of God; but our strength must be in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Proverbs

Proverbs 22:1.title: Proverbs 22:1
Proverbs 22:1.content: We should be more careful to do that by which we may get and keep a good name, than to raise or add unto a great estate.

Proverbs 22:2.title: Proverbs 22:2
Proverbs 22:2.content: Divine Providence has so ordered it, that some are rich, and others poor, but all are guilty before God; and at the throne of God's grace the poor are as welcome as the rich.

Proverbs 22:3.title: Proverbs 22:3
Proverbs 22:3.content: Faith foresees the evil coming upon sinners, and looks to Jesus Christ as the sure refuge from the storm.

Proverbs 22:4.title: Proverbs 22:4
Proverbs 22:4.content: Where the fear of God is, there will be humility. And much is to be enjoyed by it; spiritual riches, and eternal life at last.

Proverbs 22:5.title: Proverbs 22:5
Proverbs 22:5.content: The way of sin is vexatious and dangerous. But the way of duty is safe and easy.

Proverbs 22:6.title: Proverbs 22:6
Proverbs 22:6.content: Train children, not in the way they would go, that of their corrupt hearts, but in the way they should go; in which, if you love them, you would have them go. As soon as possible every child should be led to the knowledge of the Saviour.

Proverbs 22:7.title: Proverbs 22:7
Proverbs 22:7.content: This shows how important it is for every man to keep out of debt. As to the things of this life, there is a difference between the rich and the poor; but let the poor remember, it is the Lord that made the difference.

Proverbs 22:8.title: Proverbs 22:8
Proverbs 22:8.content: The power which many abuse, will soon fail them.

Proverbs 22:9.title: Proverbs 22:9
Proverbs 22:9.content: He that seeks to relieve the wants and miseries of others shall be blessed.

Proverbs 22:10.title: Proverbs 22:10
Proverbs 22:10.content: Profane scoffers and revilers disturb the peace.

Proverbs 22:11.title: Proverbs 22:11
Proverbs 22:11.content: God will be the Friend of a man in whose spirit there is no guile; this honour have all the saints.

Proverbs 22:12.title: Proverbs 22:12
Proverbs 22:12.content: God turns the counsels and designs of treacherous men to their own confusion.

Proverbs 22:13.title: Proverbs 22:13
Proverbs 22:13.content: The slothful man talks of a lion without, but considers not his real danger from the devil, that roaring lion within, and from his own slothfulness, which kills him.

Proverbs 22:14.title: Proverbs 22:14
Proverbs 22:14.content: The vile sin of licentiousness commonly besots the mind beyond recovery.

Proverbs 22:15.title: Proverbs 22:15
Proverbs 22:15.content: Sin is foolishness, it is in the heart, there is an inward inclination to sin: children bring it into the world with them; and it cleaves close to the soul. We all need to be corrected by our heavenly Father.

Proverbs 22:16.title: Proverbs 22:16
Proverbs 22:16.content: We are but stewards, and must distribute what God intrusts to our care, according to his will.

Proverbs 22:17.title: Proverbs 22:17-21
Proverbs 22:17.content: To these words, to this knowledge, the ear must be bowed down, and the heart applied by faith and love. To live a life of delight in God and dependence on him, is the foundation of all practical religion. The way to know the certainty of the word of truth, is to make conscience of our duty.

Proverbs 22:18.title: Proverbs 22:17-21
Proverbs 22:18.content: To these words, to this knowledge, the ear must be bowed down, and the heart applied by faith and love. To live a life of delight in God and dependence on him, is the foundation of all practical religion. The way to know the certainty of the word of truth, is to make conscience of our duty.

Proverbs 22:19.title: Proverbs 22:17-21
Proverbs 22:19.content: To these words, to this knowledge, the ear must be bowed down, and the heart applied by faith and love. To live a life of delight in God and dependence on him, is the foundation of all practical religion. The way to know the certainty of the word of truth, is to make conscience of our duty.

Proverbs 22:20.title: Proverbs 22:17-21
Proverbs 22:20.content: To these words, to this knowledge, the ear must be bowed down, and the heart applied by faith and love. To live a life of delight in God and dependence on him, is the foundation of all practical religion. The way to know the certainty of the word of truth, is to make conscience of our duty.

Proverbs 22:21.title: Proverbs 22:17-21
Proverbs 22:21.content: To these words, to this knowledge, the ear must be bowed down, and the heart applied by faith and love. To live a life of delight in God and dependence on him, is the foundation of all practical religion. The way to know the certainty of the word of truth, is to make conscience of our duty.

Proverbs 22:22.title: Proverbs 22:22, 23
Proverbs 22:22.content: He that robs and oppresses the poor, does so at his peril. And if men will not appear for them, God will.

Proverbs 22:23.title: Proverbs 22:22, 23
Proverbs 22:23.content: He that robs and oppresses the poor, does so at his peril. And if men will not appear for them, God will.

Proverbs 22:24.title: Proverbs 22:24, 25
Proverbs 22:24.content: Our corrupt hearts have so much tinder in them, that it is dangerous to have to do with those that throw about the sparks of their passion.

Proverbs 22:25.title: Proverbs 22:24, 25
Proverbs 22:25.content: Our corrupt hearts have so much tinder in them, that it is dangerous to have to do with those that throw about the sparks of their passion.

Proverbs 22:26.title: Proverbs 22:26, 27
Proverbs 22:26.content: Every man ought to be just to himself, and his family; those are not so, who, by folly or other carelessness, waste what they have.

Proverbs 22:27.title: Proverbs 22:26, 27
Proverbs 22:27.content: Every man ought to be just to himself, and his family; those are not so, who, by folly or other carelessness, waste what they have.

Proverbs 22:28.title: Proverbs 22:28
Proverbs 22:28.content: We are taught not to trespass on another man's right. And it is hard to find a truly industrious man. Such a man will rise. Seest thou a man diligent in the business of religion? He is likely to excel. Let us then be diligent in God's work. Proverbs

Proverbs 23:1.title: Proverbs 23:1-3
Proverbs 23:1.content: God's restraints of the appetite only say, Do thyself no harm.

Proverbs 23:2.title: Proverbs 23:1-3
Proverbs 23:2.content: God's restraints of the appetite only say, Do thyself no harm.

Proverbs 23:3.title: Proverbs 23:1-3
Proverbs 23:3.content: God's restraints of the appetite only say, Do thyself no harm.

Proverbs 23:4.title: Proverbs 23:4, 5
Proverbs 23:4.content: Be not of those that will be rich. The things of this world are not happiness and a portion for a soul; those that hold them ever so fast, cannot hold them always, cannot hold them long.

Proverbs 23:5.title: Proverbs 23:4, 5
Proverbs 23:5.content: Be not of those that will be rich. The things of this world are not happiness and a portion for a soul; those that hold them ever so fast, cannot hold them always, cannot hold them long.

Proverbs 23:6.title: Proverbs 23:6-8
Proverbs 23:6.content: Do not make thyself burdensome to any, especially those not sincere. When we are called by God to his feast, and to let our souls delight themselves, Isaiah 25:6; 55:2, we may safely partake of the Bread of life.

Proverbs 23:7.title: Proverbs 23:6-8
Proverbs 23:7.content: Do not make thyself burdensome to any, especially those not sincere. When we are called by God to his feast, and to let our souls delight themselves, Isaiah 25:6; 55:2, we may safely partake of the Bread of life.

Proverbs 23:8.title: Proverbs 23:6-8
Proverbs 23:8.content: Do not make thyself burdensome to any, especially those not sincere. When we are called by God to his feast, and to let our souls delight themselves, Isaiah 25:6; 55:2, we may safely partake of the Bread of life.

Proverbs 23:9.title: Proverbs 23:9
Proverbs 23:9.content: It is our duty to take all fit occasions to speak of Divine things; but if what a wise man says will not be heard, let him hold his peace.

Proverbs 23:10.title: Proverbs 23:10, 11
Proverbs 23:10.content: The fatherless are taken under God's special protection. He is their Redeemer, who will take their part; and he is mighty, almighty.

Proverbs 23:11.title: Proverbs 23:10, 11
Proverbs 23:11.content: The fatherless are taken under God's special protection. He is their Redeemer, who will take their part; and he is mighty, almighty.

Proverbs 23:12.title: Proverbs 23:12-16
Proverbs 23:12.content: Here is a parent instructing his child to give his mind to the Scriptures. Here is a parent encouraging his child, telling him what would be for his good. And what a comfort it would be, if herein he answered his expectation!

Proverbs 23:17.title: Proverbs 23:17, 18
Proverbs 23:17.content: The believer's expectation shall not be disappointed; the end of his trials, and of the sinner's prosperity, is at hand. Proverbs 23:19-28. The gracious Saviour who purchased pardon and peace for his people, with all the affection of a tender parent, counsels us to hear and be wise, and is ready to guide our hearts in his way. Here we have an earnest call to young people, to attend to the advice of their godly parents. If the heart be guided, the steps will be guided. Buy the truth, and sell it not; be willing to part with any thing for it. Do not part with it for pleasures, honours, riches, or any thing in this world. The heart is what the great God requires. We must not think to divide the heart between God and the world; he will have all or none. Look to the rule of God's word, the conduct of his providence, and the good examples of his people. Particular cautions are given against sins most destructive to wisdom and grace in the soul. It is really a shame to make a god of the belly. Drunkenness stupefies men, and then all goes to ruin. Licentiousness takes away the heart that should be given to God. Take heed of any approaches toward this sin, it is very hard to retreat from it. It bewitches men to their ruin. Proverbs 23:29-35. Solomon warns against drunkenness. Those that would be kept from sin, must keep from all the beginnings of it, and fear coming within reach of its allurements. Foresee the punishment, what it will at last end in, if repentance prevent not. It makes men quarrel. Drunkards wilfully make woe and sorrow for themselves. It makes men impure and insolent. The tongue grows unruly; the heart utters things contrary to reason, religion, and common civility. It stupefies and besots men. They are in danger of death, of damnation; as much exposed as if they slept upon the top of a mast, yet feel secure. They fear no peril when the terrors of the Lord are before them; they feel no pain when the judgments of God are actually upon them. So lost is a drunkard to virtue and honour, so wretchedly is his conscience seared, that he is not ashamed to say, I will seek it again. With good reason we were bid to stop before the beginning. Who that has common sense would contract a habit, or sell himself to a sin, which tends to such guilt and misery, and exposes a man every day to the danger of dying insensible, and awaking in hell? Wisdom seems in these chapters to take up the discourse as at the beginning of the book. They must be considered as the words of Christ to the sinner. Proverbs

The spirit is strengthened for the spiritual work and the spiritual warfare, by true wisdom.

Proverbs 24:30.title: Proverbs 24:30-34
Proverbs 24:30.content: See what a blessing the husbandman's calling is, and what a wilderness this earth would be without it. See what great difference there is in the management even of worldly affairs. Sloth and self-indulgence are the bane of all good. When we see fields overgrown with thorns and thistles, and the fences broken down, we see an emblem of the far more deplorable state of many souls. Every vile affection grows in men's hearts; yet they compose themselves to sleep. Let us show wisdom by doubling our diligence in every good thing. Proverbs

Proverbs 25:12.title: Proverbs 25:11, 12
Proverbs 25:12.content: A word of counsel, or reproof, rightly spoken, is especially beautiful, as fine fruit becomes still more beautiful in silver baskets.

Proverbs 25:13.title: Proverbs 25:13
