Proverbs 25:14.title: Proverbs 25:14
Proverbs 25:14.content: He who pretends to have received or given that which he never had, is like the morning cloud, that disappoints those who look for rain.

Proverbs 25:15.title: Proverbs 25:15
Proverbs 25:15.content: Be patient to bear a present hurt. Be mild to speak without passion; for persuasive language is the most effectual to prevail over the hardened mind.

Proverbs 25:16.title: Proverbs 25:16
Proverbs 25:16.content: God has given us leave to use grateful things, but we are cautioned against excess.

Proverbs 25:17.title: Proverbs 25:17
Proverbs 25:17.content: We cannot be upon good terms with our neighbours, without discretion as well as sincerity. How much better a Friend is God than any other friend! The oftener we come to him, the more welcome.

Proverbs 25:18.title: Proverbs 25:18
Proverbs 25:18.content: A false testimony is dangerous in every thing.

Proverbs 25:19.title: Proverbs 25:19
Proverbs 25:19.content: Confidence in an unfaithful man is painful and vexatious; when we put any stress on him, he not only fails, but makes us feel for it.

Proverbs 25:20.title: Proverbs 25:20
Proverbs 25:20.content: We take a wrong course if we think to relieve those in sorrow by endeavouring to make them merry.

Proverbs 25:21.title: Proverbs 25:21, 22
Proverbs 25:21.content: The precept to love even our enemies is an Old Testament commandment. Our Saviour has shown his own great example in loving us when we were enemies.

Proverbs 25:22.title: Proverbs 25:21, 22
Proverbs 25:22.content: The precept to love even our enemies is an Old Testament commandment. Our Saviour has shown his own great example in loving us when we were enemies.

Proverbs 25:23.title: Proverbs 25:23
Proverbs 25:23.content: Slanders would not be so readily spoken, if they were not readily heard. Sin, if it receives any check, becomes cowardly.

Proverbs 25:24.title: Proverbs 25:24
Proverbs 25:24.content: It is better to be alone, than to be joined to one who is a hinderance to the comfort of life.

Proverbs 25:25.title: Proverbs 25:25
Proverbs 25:25.content: Heaven is a country afar off; how refreshing is good news from thence, in the everlasting gospel, which signifies glad tidings, and in the witness of the Spirit with our spirits that we are God's children!

Proverbs 25:26.title: Proverbs 25:26
Proverbs 25:26.content: When the righteous are led into sin, it is as hurtful as if the public fountains were poisoned.

Proverbs 25:27.title: Proverbs 25:27
Proverbs 25:27.content: We must be, through grace, dead to the pleasures of sense, and also to the praises of men.

Proverbs 25:28.title: Proverbs 25:28
Proverbs 25:28.content: The man who has no command over his anger, is easily robbed of peace. Let us give up ourselves to the Lord, and pray him to put his Spirit within us, and cause us to walk in his statutes. Proverbs

Proverbs 26:1.title: Proverbs 26:1
Proverbs 26:1.content: Honour is out of season to those unworthy and unfit for it.

Proverbs 26:2.title: Proverbs 26:2
Proverbs 26:2.content: He that is cursed without cause, the curse shall do him no more harm than the bird that flies over his head.

Proverbs 26:3.title: Proverbs 26:3
Proverbs 26:3.content: Every creature must be dealt with according to its nature, but careless and profligate sinners never will be ruled by reason and persuasion. Man indeed is born like the wild ass's colt; but some, by the grace of God, are changed.

Proverbs 26:4.title: Proverbs 26:4, 5
Proverbs 26:4.content: We are to fit our remarks to the man, and address them to his conscience, so as may best end the debate.

Proverbs 26:5.title: Proverbs 26:4, 5
Proverbs 26:5.content: We are to fit our remarks to the man, and address them to his conscience, so as may best end the debate.

Proverbs 26:6.title: Proverbs 26:6-9
Proverbs 26:6.content: Fools are not fit to be trusted, nor to have any honour. Wise sayings, as a foolish man delivers and applies them, lose their usefulness.

Proverbs 26:7.title: Proverbs 26:6-9
Proverbs 26:7.content: Fools are not fit to be trusted, nor to have any honour. Wise sayings, as a foolish man delivers and applies them, lose their usefulness.

Proverbs 26:8.content: Fools are not fit to be trusted, nor to have any honour. Wise sayings, as a foolish man delivers and applies them, lose their usefulness.

Proverbs 26:9.content: Fools are not fit to be trusted, nor to have any honour. Wise sayings, as a foolish man delivers and applies them, lose their usefulness.

Proverbs 26:10.title: Proverbs 26:10
Proverbs 26:10.content: This verse may either declare how the Lord, the Creator of all men, will deal with sinners according to their guilt, or, how the powerful among men should disgrace and punish the wicked.

Proverbs 26:11.title: Proverbs 26:11
Proverbs 26:11.content: The dog is a loathsome emblem of those sinners who return to their vices, 2 Peter 2:22.

Proverbs 26:12.title: Proverbs 26:12
Proverbs 26:12.content: We see many a one who has some little sense, but is proud of it. This describes those who think their spiritual state to be good, when really it is very bad.

Proverbs 26:13.title: Proverbs 26:13
Proverbs 26:13.content: The slothful man hates every thing that requires care and labour. But it is foolish to frighten ourselves from real duties by fancied difficulties. This may be applied to a man slothful in the duties of religion.

Proverbs 26:14.title: Proverbs 26:14
Proverbs 26:14.content: Having seen the slothful man in fear of his work, here we find him in love with his ease. Bodily ease is the sad occasion of many spiritual diseases. He does not care to get forward with his business. Slothful professors turn thus. The world and the flesh are hinges on which they are hung; and though they move in a course of outward services, yet they are not the nearer to heaven.

Proverbs 26:15.title: Proverbs 26:15
Proverbs 26:15.content: The sluggard is now out of his bed, but he might have lain there, for any thing he is likely to bring to pass in his work. It is common for men who will not do their duty, to pretend they cannot. Those that are slothful in religion, will not be at the pains to feed their souls with the bread of life, nor to fetch in promised blessings by prayer.

Proverbs 26:16.title: Proverbs 26:16
Proverbs 26:16.content: He that takes pains in religion, knows he is working for a good Master, and that his labour shall not be in vain.

Proverbs 26:17.title: Proverbs 26:17
Proverbs 26:17.content: To make ourselves busy in other men's matters, is to thrust ourselves into temptation.

Proverbs 26:18.title: Proverbs 26:18, 19

Proverbs 26:19.title: Proverbs 26:18, 19
Proverbs 26:19.content: He that sins in jest, must repent in earnest, or his sin will be his ruin.

Proverbs 26:20.content: Contention heats the spirit, and puts families and societies into a flame. And that fire is commonly kindled and kept burning by whisperers and backbiters.

Proverbs 26:21.content: Contention heats the spirit, and puts families and societies into a flame. And that fire is commonly kindled and kept burning by whisperers and backbiters.

Proverbs 26:27.content: What pains men take to do mischief to others! but it is digging a pit, it is rolling a stone, hard work; and they prepare mischief to themselves.

Proverbs 26:28.title: Proverbs 26:28
Proverbs 26:28.content: There are two sorts of lies equally detestable. A slandering lie, the mischief of this every body sees. A flattering lie, which secretly works ruin. A wise man will be more afraid of a flatterer than of a slanderer. Proverbs

Proverbs 27:1.title: Proverbs 27:1
Proverbs 27:1.content: We know not what a day may bring forth. This does not forbid preparing for to-morrow, but presuming upon to-morrow. We must not put off the great work of conversion, that one thing needful.

Proverbs 27:2.title: Proverbs 27:2
Proverbs 27:2.content: There may be occasion for us to justify ourselves, but not to praise ourselves.

Proverbs 27:3.title: Proverbs 27:3, 4
Proverbs 27:3.content: Those who have no command of their passions, sink under the load.

Proverbs 27:4.title: Proverbs 27:3, 4
Proverbs 27:4.content: Those who have no command of their passions, sink under the load.

Proverbs 27:5.title: Proverbs 27:5, 6
Proverbs 27:5.content: Plain and faithful rebukes are better, not only than secret hatred, but than love which compliments in sin, to the hurt of the soul.

Proverbs 27:6.title: Proverbs 27:5, 6
Proverbs 27:6.content: Plain and faithful rebukes are better, not only than secret hatred, but than love which compliments in sin, to the hurt of the soul.

Proverbs 27:7.title: Proverbs 27:7
Proverbs 27:7.content: The poor have a better relish of their enjoyments, and are often more thankful for them, than the rich. In like manner the proud and self-sufficient disdain the gospel; but those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, find comfort from the meanest book or sermon that testifies of Christ Jesus.

Proverbs 27:8.title: Proverbs 27:8
Proverbs 27:8.content: Every man has his proper place in society, where he may be safe and comfortable.

Proverbs 27:9.title: Proverbs 27:9, 10
Proverbs 27:9.content: Depend not for relief upon a kinsman, merely for kindred's sake; apply to those who are at hand, and will help in need. But there is a Friend that sticketh closer than a brother, and let us place entire confidence in him.

Proverbs 27:10.title: Proverbs 27:9, 10
Proverbs 27:10.content: Depend not for relief upon a kinsman, merely for kindred's sake; apply to those who are at hand, and will help in need. But there is a Friend that sticketh closer than a brother, and let us place entire confidence in him.

Proverbs 27:11.title: Proverbs 27:11
Proverbs 27:11.content: An affectionate parent urges his son to prudent conduct that should gladden his heart. The good conduct of Christians is the best answer to all who find fault with the gospel.

Proverbs 27:12.title: Proverbs 27:12
Proverbs 27:12.content: Where there is temptation, if we thrust ourselves into it, there will be sin, and punishment will follow.

Proverbs 27:13.title: Proverbs 27:13
Proverbs 27:13.content: An honest man may be made a beggar, but he is not honest that makes himself one.

Proverbs 27:14.title: Proverbs 27:14
Proverbs 27:14.content: It is folly to be fond of being praised; it is a temptation to pride.

Proverbs 27:15.title: Proverbs 27:15, 16
Proverbs 27:15.content: The contentions of a neighbour may be like a sharp shower, troublesome for a time; the contentions of a wife are like constant rain.

Proverbs 27:16.title: Proverbs 27:15, 16
Proverbs 27:16.content: The contentions of a neighbour may be like a sharp shower, troublesome for a time; the contentions of a wife are like constant rain.

Proverbs 27:17.title: Proverbs 27:17
Proverbs 27:17.content: We are cautioned to take heed whom we converse with. And directed to have in view, in conversation, to make one another wiser and better.

Proverbs 27:18.title: Proverbs 27:18
Proverbs 27:18.content: Though a calling be laborious and despised, yet those who keep to it, will find there is something to be got by it. God is a Master who has engaged to honour those who serve him faithfully.

Proverbs 27:19.title: Proverbs 27:19
Proverbs 27:19.content: One corrupt heart is like another; so are sanctified hearts: the former bear the same image of the earthly, the latter the same image of the heavenly. Let us carefully watch our own hearts, comparing them with the word of God.

Proverbs 27:20.title: Proverbs 27:20
Proverbs 27:20.content: Two things are here said to be never satisfied, death and sin. The appetites of the carnal mind for profit or pleasure are always desiring more. Those whose eyes are ever toward the Lord, are satisfied in him, and shall for ever be so.

Proverbs 27:21.title: Proverbs 27:21
Proverbs 27:21.content: Silver and gold are tried by putting them into the furnace and fining-pot; so is a man tried by praising him.

Proverbs 27:22.title: Proverbs 27:22
Proverbs 27:22.content: Some are so bad, that even severe methods do not answer the end; what remains but that they should be rejected? The new-creating power of God's grace alone is able to make a change.

Proverbs 27:23.title: Proverbs 27:23-27
Proverbs 27:23.content: We ought to have some business to do in this world, and not to live in idleness, and not to meddle with what we do not understand. We must be diligent and take pains. Let us do what we can, still the world cannot be secured to us, therefore we must choose a more lasting portion; but by the blessing of God upon our honest labours, we may expect to enjoy as much of earthly blessings as is good for us. Proverbs 27:24.content: We ought to have some business to do in this world, and not to live in idleness, and not to meddle with what we do not understand. We must be diligent and take pains. Proverbs

Proverbs 28:1.title: Proverbs 28:1
Proverbs 28:1.content: Sin makes men cowards. Whatever difficulties the righteous meet in the way of duty, they are not daunted.

Proverbs 28:2.title: Proverbs 28:2
Proverbs 28:2.content: National sins disturb the public repose.

Proverbs 28:3.title: Proverbs 28:3
Proverbs 28:3.content: If needy persons get opportunities of oppressing, their extortion will be more severe than that of the more wealthy.

Proverbs 28:4.title: Proverbs 28:4
Proverbs 28:4.content: Wicked people strengthen one another in wicked ways.

Proverbs 28:5.title: Proverbs 28:5
Proverbs 28:5.content: If a man seeks the Lord, it is a good sign that he understands much, and it is a good means of understanding more.

Proverbs 28:6.title: Proverbs 28:6
Proverbs 28:6.content: An honest, godly, poor man, is better than a wicked, ungodly, rich man; has more comfort in himself, and is a greater blessing to the world.

Proverbs 28:7.title: Proverbs 28:7
Proverbs 28:7.content: Companions of riotous men not only grieve their parents, but shame them.

Proverbs 28:8.title: Proverbs 28:8
Proverbs 28:8.content: That which is ill got, though it may increase much, will not last long. Thus the poor are repaid, and God is glorified.

Proverbs 28:9.title: Proverbs 28:9
Proverbs 28:9.content: The sinner at whose prayers God is angry, is one who obstinately refuses to obey God's commands.

Proverbs 28:10.title: Proverbs 28:10
Proverbs 28:10.content: The success of ungodly men is their own misery.

Proverbs 28:11.title: Proverbs 28:11
Proverbs 28:11.content: Rich men are so flattered, that they think themselves superior to others.

Proverbs 28:12.title: Proverbs 28:12
Proverbs 28:12.content: There is glory in the land when the righteous have liberty.

Proverbs 28:13.title: Proverbs 28:13
Proverbs 28:13.content: It is folly to indulge sin, and excuse it. He who covers his sins, shall not have any true peace. He who humbly confesses his sins, with true repentance and faith, shall find mercy from God. The Son of God is our great atonement. Under a deep sense of our guilt and danger, we may claim salvation from that mercy which reigns through righteousness unto eternal life, by Jesus Christ our Lord.

Proverbs 28:14.title: Proverbs 28:14
Proverbs 28:14.content: There is a fear which causes happiness. Faith and love will deliver from the fear of eternal misery; but we should always fear offending God, and fear sinning against him.

Proverbs 28:15.title: Proverbs 28:15
Proverbs 28:15.content: A wicked ruler, whatever we may call him, this scripture calls a roaring lion, and a ranging bear.

Proverbs 28:16.title: Proverbs 28:16
Proverbs 28:16.content: Oppressors want understanding; they do not consult their own honour, ease, and safety.

Proverbs 28:17.title: Proverbs 28:17
Proverbs 28:17.content: The murderer shall be haunted with terrors. None shall desire to save him from deserved punishment, nor pity him.

Proverbs 28:18.title: Proverbs 28:18
Proverbs 28:18.content: Uprightness will give men holy security in the worst times; but the false and dishonest are never safe.

Proverbs 28:19.title: Proverbs 28:19
Proverbs 28:19.content: Those who are diligent, take the way to live comfortably.

Proverbs 28:20.title: Proverbs 28:20
Proverbs 28:20.content: The true way to be happy, is to be holy and honest; not to raise an estate suddenly, without regard to right or wrong.

Proverbs 28:21.title: Proverbs 28:21
Proverbs 28:21.content: Judgment is perverted, when any thing but pure right is considered.

Proverbs 28:22.title: Proverbs 28:22
Proverbs 28:22.content: He that hastens to be rich, never seriously thinks how quickly God may take his wealth from him, and leave him in poverty.

Proverbs 28:23.title: Proverbs 28:23
Proverbs 28:23.content: Upon reflection, most will have a better opinion of a faithful reprover than of a soothing flatterer.

Proverbs 28:24.title: Proverbs 28:24
Proverbs 28:24.content: Here is the wickedness of those who think it no sin to rob their parents, by wheedling them or threatening them, or by wasting what they have, and running into debt.

Proverbs 28:25.title: Proverbs 28:25
Proverbs 28:25.content: Those make themselves always easy, that live in continual dependence upon God and his grace, and live by faith.

Proverbs 28:26.title: Proverbs 28:26
Proverbs 28:26.content: A fool trusts to his own strength, merit, and righteousness. And trusts to his own heart, which is not only deceitful above all things, but which has often deceived him.

Proverbs 28:27.title: Proverbs 28:27
Proverbs 28:27.content: A selfish man not only will not look out for objects of compassion, but will look off from those that call for his attention.

Proverbs 28:28.title: Proverbs 28:28
Proverbs 28:28.content: When power is put into the hands of the wicked, wise men decline public business. If the reader will go diligently over this and the other chapters, in many places where at first he may suppose there is least of Christ, still he will find what will lead to him. Proverbs

Proverbs 29:1.title: Proverbs 29:1
Proverbs 29:1.content: If God wounds, who can heal? The word of God warns all to flee from the wrath to come, to the hope set before us in Jesus Christ.

Proverbs 29:2.title: Proverbs 29:2
Proverbs 29:2.content: The people have cause to rejoice or mourn, as their rulers are righteous or wicked.

Proverbs 29:3.title: Proverbs 29:3
Proverbs 29:3.content: Divine wisdom best keeps us from ruinous lusts.

Proverbs 29:4.title: Proverbs 29:4
Proverbs 29:4.content: The Lord Jesus is the King who will minister true judgment to the people.

Proverbs 29:5.title: Proverbs 29:5
Proverbs 29:5.content: Flatterers put men off their guard, which betrays them into foolish conduct.

Proverbs 29:6.title: Proverbs 29:6
Proverbs 29:6.content: Transgressions always end in vexations. Righteous men walk at liberty, and walk in safety.

Proverbs 29:7.title: Proverbs 29:7
Proverbs 29:7.content: This verse is applicable to compassion for the distress of the poor, and the unfeeling disregard shown by the wicked.

Proverbs 29:8.title: Proverbs 29:8
Proverbs 29:8.content: The scornful mock at things sacred and serious. Men who promote religion, which is true wisdom, turn away the wrath of God.

Proverbs 29:9.title: Proverbs 29:9
Proverbs 29:9.content: If a wise man dispute with a conceited wrangler, he will be treated with anger or ridicule; and no good is done.

Proverbs 29:10.title: Proverbs 29:10
Proverbs 29:10.content: Christ told his disciples that they should be hated of all men. The just, whom the blood-thirsty hate, gladly do any thing for their salvation.

Proverbs 29:11.title: Proverbs 29:11
Proverbs 29:11.content: He is a fool who tells every thing he knows, and can keep no counsel.

Proverbs 29:12.title: Proverbs 29:12
Proverbs 29:12.content: One who loves flatterers, and hearkens to slanderers, causes his servants to become liars and false accusers.

Proverbs 29:13.title: Proverbs 29:13
Proverbs 29:13.content: Some are poor, others have a great deal of deceitful riches. They meet in the business of this world; the Lord gives to both the comforts of this life. To some of both sorts he gives his grace.

Proverbs 29:14.title: Proverbs 29:14
Proverbs 29:14.content: The rich will look to themselves, but the poor and needy the prince must defend and plead for.

Proverbs 29:15.title: Proverbs 29:15
Proverbs 29:15.content: Parents must consider the benefit of due correction, and the mischief of undue indulgence.

Proverbs 29:16.title: Proverbs 29:16
Proverbs 29:16.content: Let not the righteous have their faith and hope shocked by the increase of sin and sinners, but let them wait with patience.

Proverbs 29:17.title: Proverbs 29:17
Proverbs 29:17.content: Children must not be suffered to go without rebuke when they do amiss.

Proverbs 29:18.title: Proverbs 29:18
Proverbs 29:18.content: How bare does a place look without Bibles and ministers! and what an easy prey is it to the enemy of souls! That gospel is an open vision, which holds forth Christ, which humbles the sinner and exalts the Saviour, which promotes holiness in the life and conversation: and these are precious truths to keep the soul alive, and prevent it from perishing.

Proverbs 29:19.title: Proverbs 29:19
Proverbs 29:19.content: Here is an unprofitable, slothful, wicked servant; one that serves not from conscience, or love, but from fear.

Proverbs 29:20.title: Proverbs 29:20
Proverbs 29:20.content: When a man is self-conceited, rash, and given to wrangling, there is more hope of the ignorant and profligate.

Proverbs 29:21.title: Proverbs 29:21
Proverbs 29:21.content: Good usage to a servant does not mean indulgence, which would ruin even a child. The body is a servant to the soul; those that humour it, and are over-tender of it, will find it forget its place.

Proverbs 29:22.title: Proverbs 29:22
Proverbs 29:22.content: An angry, passionate disposition makes men provoking to one another, and provoking to God.

Proverbs 29:23.title: Proverbs 29:23
Proverbs 29:23.content: Only those who humble themselves shall be exalted and established.

Proverbs 29:24.title: Proverbs 29:24
Proverbs 29:24.content: The receiver is as bad as the thief.

Proverbs 29:25.title: Proverbs 29:25
Proverbs 29:25.content: Many are ashamed to own Christ now; and he will not own them in the day of judgment. But he that trusts in the Lord will be saved from this snare.

Proverbs 29:26.title: Proverbs 29:26
Proverbs 29:26.content: The wisest course is, to look to God, and seek the favour of the Ruler of rulers; for every creature is that to us which God makes it to be.

Proverbs 29:27.title: Proverbs 29:27
Proverbs 29:27.content: The just man abhors the sins of the wicked, and shuns their company. Christ exposed the wickedness of men, yet prayed for the wicked when they were crucifying him. Hatred to sin in ourselves and others, is a needful branch of the Christian temper. But all that are unholy, have rooted hatred to godliness. Proverbs

Proverbs 30:1.title: Proverbs 30:1-6
Proverbs 30:1.content: Agur speaks of himself as wanting a righteousness, and having done very foolishly. And it becomes us all to have low thoughts of ourselves. He speaks of himself as wanting revelation to guide him in the ways of truth and wisdom. The more enlightened people are, the more they lament their ignorance; the more they pray for clearer, still clearer discoveries of God, and his rich grace in Christ Jesus. In ver.

Proverbs 30:4.title: Proverbs 30:4
Proverbs 30:4.content: In every age there are monsters of ingratitude who ill-treat their parents. Many persuade themselves they are holy persons, whose hearts are full of sin, and who practise secret wickedness. There are others whose lofty pride is manifest. There have also been cruel monsters in every age.

Proverbs 30:15.title: Proverbs 30:15-17
Proverbs 30:15.content: Cruelty and covetousness are two daughters of the horseleech, that still cry, "Give, give," and they are continually uneasy to themselves. Four things never are satisfied, to which these devourers are compared. Those are never rich that are always coveting. And many who have come to a bad end, have owned that their wicked courses began by despising their parents' authority.

Proverbs 30:16.title: Proverbs 30:15-17
Proverbs 30:16.content: Cruelty and covetousness are two daughters of the horseleech, that still cry, "Give, give," and they are continually uneasy to themselves. Four things never are satisfied, to which these devourers are compared. Those are never rich that are always coveting. And many who have come to a bad end, have owned that their wicked courses began by despising their parents' authority.

Proverbs 30:18.title: Proverbs 30:18-20
Proverbs 30:18.content: Four things cannot be fully known. The kingdom of nature is full of marvels. The fourth is a mystery of iniquity; the cursed arts by which a vile seducer gains the affections of a female; and the arts which a vile woman uses to conceal her wickedness.

Proverbs 30:19.title: Proverbs 30:18-20
Proverbs 30:19.content: Four things cannot be fully known. The kingdom of nature is full of marvels. The fourth is a mystery of iniquity; the cursed arts by which a vile seducer gains the affections of a female; and the arts which a vile woman uses to conceal her wickedness.

Proverbs 30:20.title: Proverbs 30:18-20
Proverbs 30:20.content: Four things cannot be fully known. The kingdom of nature is full of marvels. The fourth is a mystery of iniquity; the cursed arts by which a vile seducer gains the affections of a female; and the arts which a vile woman uses to conceal her wickedness.

Proverbs 30:21.title: Proverbs 30:21-23
Proverbs 30:21.content: Four things that are little, are yet to be admired. There are those who are poor in the world, and of small account, yet wise for their souls and another world.

Proverbs 30:22.title: Proverbs 30:21-23
Proverbs 30:22.content: Four things that are little, are yet to be admired. There are those who are poor in the world, and of small account, yet wise for their souls and another world.

Proverbs 30:23.title: Proverbs 30:21-23
Proverbs 30:23.content: Four things that are little, are yet to be admired. There are those who are poor in the world, and of small account, yet wise for their souls and another world.

Proverbs 30:29.title: Proverbs 30:29-33
Proverbs 30:29.content: We may learn from animals to go well; also to keep our temper under all provocations. We must keep the evil thought in our minds from breaking out into evil speeches. We must not stir up the passions of others. Let nothing be said or done with violence, but every thing with softness and calmness. Alas, how often have we done foolishly in rising up against the Lord our King! Let us humble ourselves before him. And having found peace with Him, let us follow peace with all men. Proverbs 31 An exhortation to king Lemuel to take heed of sin, and to do duties. (1-9) The description of a virtuous woman. (10-31)

Proverbs 31:1.title: Proverbs 31:1-9
Proverbs 31:1.content: When children are under the mother's eye, she has an opportunity of fashioning their minds aright. Those who are grown up, should often call to mind the good teaching they received when children. The many awful instances of promising characters who have been ruined by vile women, and love of wine, should warn every one to avoid these evils. Wine is to be used for want or medicine. Every creature of God is good, and wine, though abused, has its use. By the same rule, due praise and consolation should be used as cordials to the dejected and tempted, not administered to the confident and self-sufficient. All in authority should be more carefully temperate even than other men; and should be protectors of those who are unable or afraid to plead their own cause. Our blessed Lord did not decline the bitterest dregs of the cup of sorrow put into his hands; but he puts the cup of consolation into the hands of his people, and causes those to rejoice who are in the deepest distress.

Proverbs 31:3.title: Proverbs 31:1-9
Proverbs 31:3.content: When children are under the mother's eye, she has an opportunity of fashioning their minds aright. Those who are grown up, should often call to mind the good teaching they received when children. The many awful instances of promising characters who have been ruined by vile women, and love of wine, should warn every one to avoid these evils. Wine is to be used for want or medicine. Every creature of God is good, and wine, though abused, has its use. By the same rule, due praise and consolation should be used as cordials to the dejected and tempted, not administered to the confident and self-sufficient. All in authority should be more carefully temperate even than other men; and should be protectors of those who are unable or afraid to plead their own cause. Our blessed Lord did not decline the bitterest dregs of the cup of sorrow put into his hands; but he puts the cup of consolation into the hands of his people, and causes those to rejoice who are in the deepest distress.

Proverbs 31:10.title: Proverbs 31:10-31
Proverbs 31:10.content: This is the description of a virtuous woman of those days, but the general outlines equally suit every age and nation. She is very careful to recommend herself to her husband's esteem and affection, to know his mind, and is willing that he rule over her. 1. She can be trusted, and he will leave such a wife to manage for him. He is happy in her. And she makes it her constant business to do him good. 2. She is one that takes pains in her duties, and takes pleasure in them. She is careful to fill up time, that none be lost. She rises early. She applies herself to the business proper for her, to women's business. She does what she does, with all her power, and trifles not. 3. She makes what she does turn to good account by prudent management. Many undo themselves by buying, without considering whether they can afford it. She provides well for her house. She lays up for hereafter. 4. She looks well to the ways of her household, that she may oblige all to do their duty to God and one another, as well as to her. 5. She is intent upon giving as upon getting, and does it freely and cheerfully. 6. She is discreet and obliging; every word she says, shows she governs herself by the rules of wisdom. She not only takes prudent measures herself, but gives prudent advice to others. The law of love and kindness is written in the heart, and shows itself in the tongue. Her heart is full of another world, even when her hands are most busy about this world. 7. Above all, she fears the Lord. Beauty recommends none to God, nor is it any proof of wisdom and goodness, but it has deceived many a man who made his choice of a wife by it. But the fear of God reigning in the heart, is the beauty of the soul; it lasts for ever. 8. She has firmness to bear up under crosses and disappointments. She shall reflect with comfort when she comes to be old, that she was not idle or useless when young. She shall rejoice in a world to come. She is a great blessing to her relations. If the fruit be good, the tree must have our good word. But she leaves it to her own works to praise her. Every one ought to desire this honour that cometh from God; and according to this standard we all ought to regulate our judgments. This description let all women daily study, who desire to be truly beloved and respected, useful and honourable. This passage is to be applied to individuals, but may it not also be applied to the church of God, which is described as a virtuous spouse? God by his grace has formed from among sinful men a church of true believers, to possess all the excellences here described. Ecclesiastes Ecclesiastes 1 Solomon shows that all human things are vain. (1-3) Man's toil and want of satisfaction. (4-8) There is nothing new. (9-11) The vexation in pursuit of knowledge. (12-18)

Proverbs 31:31.content: This is the description of a virtuous woman of those days, but the general outlines equally suit every age and nation. She is very careful to recommend herself to her husband's esteem and affection, to know his mind, and is willing that he rule over her. 1. She can be trusted, and he will leave such a wife to manage for him. He is happy in her. And she makes it her constant business to do him good. 2. She is one that takes pains in her duties, and takes pleasure in them. She is careful to fill up time, that none be lost. She rises early. She applies herself to the business proper for her, to women's business. She does what she does, with all her power, and trifles not. 3.
